2764.content:
# Career
Law is a profession of great demand in India, and all around the world. The rising demand for lawyers is fuelled by the changing social and economic circumstances and the ever-increasing regulatory role of the government. The legal profession in India has undergone a strategic and substantial change over the last few decades. Law aspirants not only distinguish themselves in courts but mark their presence in various corporate houses, law agencies, law firms, litigation, NGOs and administrative services.
2764.title: Career

2765.content:
# Career

Since a lawyer holds a great responsibility in moulding society, legal education plays a major role in shaping society at large. Legal education trains individuals on principles, philosophies, ethics, history, and ideologies. An individual should be aware of the society he is intending to start practice in. The lawyer should acquire the fullest knowledge of the constitution and culture during the course period. A lawyer who develops perseverance becomes a great lawyer. Legal education also inculcates analytical abilities, research abilities, and logical thinking, judgment, and communication skills.
2765.title: Career

2766.content:
# Career

School of Law at GD Goenka University offers 3 years LL.B (Hons.) Degree as well as 5 Years integrated Law degree programmes such as BA-LLB(Hons.) & BBA-LLB(Hons.). These Degree Programmes are offered in various Specializations such as Constitutional Law, Criminal Law, and Corporate Law & Arbitration. School of Law also offers 1 Year LL.M Degree Programme with Specialization in Constitutional Law, Criminal Law, Corporate Law, Arbitration Law & IPR. Training students in these specialized courses will prepare them for jobs as Associate Partner in corporate Law Firms, Patent Attorney, Tax Lawyer, Legal Advisor in Banks, PSUs, LPOs etc. to name a few.
2766.title: Career

2767.content:
### Career Pathway
##### Advocacy
Advocacy is one of the chief professions chosen by LLB graduates. Students choosing this path can practice in the courts. After qualifying the examination conducted by the All India Bar council, they enrol with All India Bar Council; they can opt to practice in any court across the country. Basic salaries for fresher’s start from 15,000/- per month whereas experienced lawyers can earn more than 1 lakh per month. These salaries are for lawyers practicing in the lower courts. Supreme Court lawyers earn as much as INR 50,00,000 for an appearance!
##### Legal Advisor
2767.title: Career

2768.content:
### Career Pathway

##### Legal Advisor
After completing your LLB, you can become a legal analyst or join Law Firms, Private Companies, Corporate firms or Banks. Most large corporations and government organizations hire legal advisors. Banks like ICICI bank also pay in equal measures. The typical compensation is 10L for fresh graduates. You can provide advice on various legal matters and become in-house counsel. Furthermore, your legal expertise could also be used in NGOs. You can choose to become the legal advisor or in-house counsel and help the company with legal decisions. A lawyer can get an MBA after their LLB. This ensures a rewarding career in the C-Suite. Law graduates conduct analyses regarding the law sphere about the company and its functions.
##### Corporate Lawyer
2768.title: Career

2769.content:
### Career Pathway

##### Corporate Lawyer
Corporate lawyers take home handsome compensation. The tier two firms such as Desai and Diwanji, Nishith Desai Associates (NDA), Wadia Ghandy and Co., Kochhar, and Co., Bharucha Partners, etc. pay between INR 40,000/month and INR 80,000/month. The top firms currently offer compensation packages of up to 14L per year for fresh associates. Some of the much sort after firms are Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas, AZB, Jyoti Sagar Associates (JSA), Trilegal, Khaitan and Company, Luthra & Luthra and S & R Associates. Compensation rises with seniority and partners typically have a compensation of 1Cr.
##### Government Services
2769.title: Career

2770.content:
### Career Pathway

##### Government Services
By clearing exams conducted by Public Service Commissions, a law graduate can become a judge. After gaining experience, a law graduate can hope to become Solicitor General, a Public Prosecutor or offer services to government departments and ministries. One can also work as a legal adviser for various Govt. Organisations. The prestige and respect accorded by society is unmatched.
##### Career Abroad
Legal education in India is similar to the one in Britain. Whereas several universities in UK offer legal education to Indian students, Indians after appearing for the Bar in the UK practice in the UK courts.
##### Judicial Services
2770.title: Career

2771.content:
### Career Pathway

##### Judicial Services
Students are also free to work for the judicial machinery of Country as a Judge or Magistrate. This requires them to pass a judicial Services examination conducted by the Public Service Commission. Careers start as Magistrate, Sub-judge, or Munsif and the recruitments are through the Public Service Commission or under the supervision of the High Court. The Magistrate judges the Criminal cases and a Sub Judge decides the Civil Cases. Through promotion, these judges could become district judges and also attain higher posts the pinnacle of which is the Chief Justice of India.
##### Legal Analyst
Law graduates could join law firms or corporate firms and conduct analyses regarding the law sphere about the company and its functions. Legal Analysts also participate in drafting various legal documents and assist attorneys in filing them with the registry of the courts.
##### Legal Researcher
2771.title: Career

2772.content:
### Career Pathway

##### Legal Researcher
A legal researcher is responsible for researching various cases and helping lawyers get a deeper insight into the past cases for precedent and understanding legal nuances.
##### Career in Arbitration
Arbitration enables opposing parties to settle a dispute out of court. An arbitrator, working independently or as part of a small panel, holds hearings, reviews evidence and renders decisions. These proceedings are similar to a trial, but more private and less formal. Since the decisions through Arbitration is faster, resolution of corporate disputes are usually pursued through this path. Earning a bachelor’s degree is the first step toward a career in arbitration. Highly experienced lawyers or business professionals with extensive knowledge of a particular industry or body of law are appointed as Arbitrators and is highly lucrative. Arbitration specialties include construction, real estate, insurance and labour relations.
##### Teaching
2772.title: Career

2773.content:
### Career Pathway

##### Teaching
On completion of your LLM and you have a flair for explaining and narrating different topics to a group of people then you could join as a faculty member in a University.

### VIII GD Goenka - CIArb (India) International Commercial Arbitration Moot Competition 2026

# CIArb
#### VIII GD Goenka - CIArb (India) International Commercial Arbitration Moot Competition 2026: Registrations Open
The School of Law, GD Goenka University, in partnership with The Chartered Institute of Arbitrators (CIArb) - India, The Society of Indian Law Firms (SILF), and The International Centre for Dispute Resolution (ICDR) - Singapore, invites law students from across the globe to participate in the VIII GD Goenka - CIArb (India) International Commercial Arbitration Moot Competition 2026.
The competition will be held offline from 25th to 27th September 2026 at the GD Goenka University campus in Sohna, Gurugram, Haryana. With a total prize pool exceeding INR 6,00,000, the moot promises to be a premier platform for aspiring arbitration advocates.
2774.title: CIArb

2775.content:
#### About the Competition
Now in its eighth edition, this flagship event of the GD Goenka School of Law continues its legacy of fostering excellence in advocacy and arbitration practice. The competition is designed to simulate authentic arbitral proceedings, providing participants with the opportunity to argue before seasoned arbitrators and practitioners. This year's edition places a special focus on the evolving and increasingly crucial domain of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) considerations in international commercial arbitration. By placing this critical theme at the heart of the competition, the organisers aim to equip students with the legal acumen and practical insights necessary to navigate the intersection of commercial interests and contemporary global sustainability practices.
2775.title: CIArb

2776.content:
#### About GD Goenka University & School of Law
GD Goenka University, established in 2013, is a modern, multidisciplinary institution located in the GD Goenka Education City on the Sohna-Gurugram corridor. Recognised by the University Grants Commission and approved by relevant professional bodies, the University has been awarded an A+ grade by NAAC.
The School of Law at GD Goenka University combines an advanced academic curriculum with experiential legal training, offering undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes covering a broad spectrum of legal fields including international commercial arbitration and investment arbitration. The School of Law was ranked as the "No. 1 Promising Law School in India" by the Competition Success Review (CSR) Law Schools Survey in 2025.
2776.title: CIArb

2777.content:
#### Supporting Organisations
 * The Chartered Institute of Arbitrators (CIArb) - India: A globally recognised centre of excellence dedicated to the practice and profession of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), with over 17,000 professionals across 149 countries.
 * The Society of Indian Law Firms (SILF): The collective body of India's leading corporate law firms, with over 100 member firms, working to advance the interests of the legal community.
 * The International Centre for Dispute Resolution (ICDR) - Singapore: The international division of the American Arbitration Association (AAA), widely recognised as a leading provider of efficient cross-border dispute resolution services.

#### Eligibility
Undergraduate or postgraduate students of law from any recognised institution are eligible to participate. Only one team will be allowed to participate from a single institution.

2798.content:
### Geographical Indications International Conference

The School of Law, GD Goenka University successfully organized the International Conference on “Geographical Indications: Institutions, Technology, Entrepreneurship, and Social Impact” on 10–11 April 2026. The two-day conference brought together academicians, legal experts, researchers, entrepreneurs, policymakers, artisans, and students to deliberate upon the growing significance of Geographical Indications (GIs) in preserving cultural heritage, promoting innovation, and strengthening local economies.
2798.title: Geographical Indications International Conference

2799.content:
### Geographical Indications International Conference

The conference featured 12 thematic tracks covering diverse areas related to Geographical Indications, including intellectual property rights, traditional knowledge protection, sustainable development, rural entrepreneurship, digital technology and GI protection, trade and commerce, agricultural innovations, cultural preservation, handicrafts, textiles, and socio-economic impact. The sessions encouraged interdisciplinary discussions and provided a platform for participants to exchange ideas, research findings, and policy perspectives on the evolving role of GIs in India and globally.
2799.title: Geographical Indications International Conference

2800.content:
### Geographical Indications International Conference

One of the major highlights of the conference was the vibrant exhibition organized alongside the academic sessions. Local artisans and entrepreneurs from Rajasthan, Haryana, and several other states showcased a wide variety of traditional products and crafts that reflected India’s rich cultural diversity and craftsmanship. The exhibition included handicrafts, handloom products, traditional fabrics and textiles, agricultural tools, pottery, artwork, and various indigenous products associated with regional identities and heritage.
The exhibition provided artisans with an opportunity to interact directly with scholars, industry experts, and visitors, thereby promoting awareness regarding the importance of protecting traditional products through Geographical Indications. It also emphasized the role of GI tags in empowering local communities, preserving indigenous knowledge, and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities.
2800.title: Geographical Indications International Conference

2801.content:
### Geographical Indications International Conference

The conference successfully created a meaningful dialogue between academia, industry, and grassroots communities. Through its scholarly deliberations and cultural exhibitions, the event highlighted the importance of Geographical Indications as a tool for economic development, entrepreneurship, social inclusion, and preservation of traditional heritage in an increasingly globalized world.
2801.title: Geographical Indications International Conference

### Guest Lecture on Women Empowerment

The School of Law, GD Goenka University organized an enriching guest lecture on 1 April 2026 on the theme of “Women Empowerment” for the students of BA LL.B. (Hons.). The session was delivered by Dr. B. Rajeshwari, who is associated with Azad Foundation. The lecture aimed to provide students with practical insights into women empowerment initiatives, policy-making processes, and the role of non-governmental organizations in promoting gender equality and social justice.
During the session, Dr. Rajeshwari shared her experiences and expertise in the field of policy advocacy and grassroots empowerment. She discussed the importance of inclusive policy-making and highlighted how organizations working at the grassroots level contribute significantly towards creating opportunities for marginalized women. The lecture focused on the practical challenges faced by women in society and the need for sustainable measures to ensure their social and economic independence.
2807.title: Guest Lecture On Women Empowerment

2808.content:
### Guest Lecture on Women Empowerment

A major highlight of the session was the discussion on the initiatives undertaken by Azad Foundation, particularly the “Women on Wheels” programme. Dr. Rajeshwari explained how the organization trains women in professional driving skills, enabling them to become financially independent and self-reliant. She elaborated on how such initiatives not only create employment opportunities but also challenge traditional gender stereotypes and promote confidence among women.
The session was highly interactive, and students actively participated by asking questions and engaging in meaningful discussions on gender justice, empowerment, and social change. The lecture provided students with a practical understanding of how law, policy, and social initiatives collectively contribute towards women empowerment.
2808.title: Guest Lecture On Women Empowerment

2809.content:
### Guest Lecture on Women Empowerment

Overall, the guest lecture proved to be informative and inspiring, encouraging students to develop a socially sensitive and inclusive perspective towards issues concerning women and community development.

### Trial Advocacy & Courtroom Procedures

The School of Law, GD Goenka University organized an insightful and practice-oriented session on “Fundamentals and Procedure of Trial Advocacy” on 17 March and 31 March 2026. The sessions were conducted by Advocate Simarjeet Singh Satia, who shared his extensive practical experience and expertise in the field of trial advocacy and courtroom procedures.
The primary objective of the sessions was to familiarize law students with the essential principles, techniques, and practical aspects involved in trial advocacy. The sessions provided participants with a comprehensive understanding of courtroom conduct, stages of trial, client interaction, framing of arguments, examination and cross-examination of witnesses, presentation of evidence, and advocacy skills required for effective legal practice.
2810.title: Trial Advocacy Courtroom Procedures

2811.content:
### Trial Advocacy & Courtroom Procedures

Advocate Simarjeet Singh Satia emphasized the importance of preparation, legal research, communication skills, and ethical conduct in courtroom proceedings. Through practical examples and interactive discussions, he explained the procedural aspects of both civil and criminal trials, enabling students to bridge the gap between theoretical legal education and real courtroom practice. The sessions also highlighted the role of confidence, articulation, and strategic thinking in developing effective advocacy skills.
Students actively participated in the discussions and engaged in exercises related to courtroom presentation and trial procedures. The interactive nature of the sessions encouraged students to ask questions and gain clarity regarding practical challenges faced by advocates during trials. The resource person also shared valuable insights on professional responsibilities, courtroom etiquette, and the evolving role of advocates in the justice delivery system.
2811.title: Trial Advocacy Courtroom Procedures

2812.content:

The sessions proved to be highly informative and beneficial for aspiring legal professionals. By focusing on practical learning and skill development, the programme significantly contributed towards enhancing students’ understanding of trial procedures and advocacy techniques. The event reflected the School of Law’s commitment to providing experiential legal education and preparing students for the professional demands of the legal field.

2819.content:
### Think Tank Discussion

The Faculty Think Tank of the School of Law organized an insightful discussion session on 28 February 2026 on the topic, “From Tariffs to Trust: A New Era for India–US Relations Amidst the 2026 Trade Deal.” The session aimed to analyze the evolving economic and strategic partnership between India and the United States in light of the recently proposed trade developments and their broader geopolitical implications.
The discussion was led by the distinguished discussants, Mr. Afeef Abdul Kader and Mr. Tushar Sharma, who provided a comprehensive understanding of the changing dynamics in India–US bilateral relations. The session highlighted how the 2026 trade deal signifies a transition from traditional tariff-based negotiations to a relationship built on mutual trust, strategic cooperation, and economic collaboration.
2819.title: Think Tank Discussion

2820.content:
### Think Tank Discussion

The discussants explored various dimensions of the trade agreement, including market access, digital trade, technology transfer, supply chain resilience, and investment opportunities. Special emphasis was laid on the potential benefits of the agreement for India’s economic growth, employment generation, and global trade positioning. The speakers also discussed the challenges associated with balancing domestic economic interests while strengthening international partnerships.
The session encouraged faculty members and participants to critically examine the role of international trade agreements in shaping foreign policy and global governance. The deliberations also reflected upon the broader strategic partnership between India and the United States in areas such as defense cooperation, innovation, climate initiatives, and regional security.
2820.title: Think Tank Discussion

2821.content:
### Think Tank Discussion

The discussion proved to be highly engaging and intellectually stimulating, fostering meaningful dialogue among participants on contemporary international economic issues. The event successfully fulfilled the objectives of the Faculty Think Tank by promoting academic discourse, policy-oriented analysis, and informed understanding of current global developments affecting India’s international relations and trade policies.
2821.title: Think Tank Discussion

# Career
### Discover Your Future with GD Goenka University: Empowering BBA, MBA, and B.Com Graduates
Are you ready to take the first step toward an extraordinary career? At GD Goenka University, we don’t just teach—you grow, evolve, and prepare to conquer the professional world. Whether your passion lies in managing global business operations, designing innovative marketing campaigns, or mastering the complexities of finance, our BBA, MBA, and B.Com programs are the perfect launchpads to turn your dreams into reality. With cutting-edge learning, real-world exposure, and a proven track record of success, we’re here to help you achieve greatness.
2916.title: Career

2917.content:
### Why Choose GD Goenka University?
Our unique approach integrates rigorous academics, industry interactions, and skill enhancement to ensure our graduates stand out. Here’s how we help you thrive:
 * **Industrial Visits for Practical Exposure:** Gain hands-on insights into corporate operations through visits to top organizations like Honda and IOTECH.
 * **Skill Enhancement and VAC Courses:** Specialized workshops and Value-Added Certifications in areas like business analytics, digital marketing, and financial planning ensure industry relevance.
 * **Guest Lectures and Networking Opportunities:** Learn directly from leaders at IBM, KPMG, and Ernst & Young through events like “Coffee with Corporates” and interactive guest sessions.
 * **Internships and Real-World Experience:** Mandatory internships provide the perfect platform to apply classroom learning to practical scenarios.

### Career Pathway
##### Unlock Diverse Career Pathways
 * BBA Graduates: Step into roles like Customer Service Associate, Marketing Associate, or Business Analyst, excelling in fields that blend creativity and strategy. Gain expertise in retail management, human resources, or financial operations to build your future.
 * MBA Graduates: Prepare for leadership roles such as Brand Manager, Financial Analyst, or Operations Manager. Explore global opportunities in fields like business intelligence, sales, and human resources while driving impactful results for top organizations.
 * B. Com Graduates: Master the financial world with careers as Tax Advisors, Auditors, or Risk Assessors. Advance into high-stakes roles like Financial Trader or Consultant, leveraging your analytical skills to navigate complex business environments.

###### 17 Feb, 2026
### Guest Lecture on Data-driven Operations for Business Excellence

**Speaker:** Mr. Prasoon Singh, Director of Business Operation and Management, Capgemini – India
**Venue:** GD Goenka University, School of Management (SOM)
**Date:** February 17
**Organized by:** School of Management, Operation and Business Analytics Area & Byte Brigade Club
## Opening Ceremony
The event commenced with a warm welcome for Mr. Prasoon Singh, led by Afsheen and Anil. Following the introduction, Dr. Smitha Girija, the Dean of the School of Management, was invited to the stage to formally thank the guest for his presence. As a gesture of sustainability and gratitude, the university presented Mr. Singh with a plant pot before the technical session began.
2951.title: Guest Lecture On Data Driven Operations For Business Excellence

2952.content:
## Interactive Session: Q&A Highlights
The core of the lecture was conducted as an interactive Q&A session moderated by Mayra and Amrit. Mr. Singh shared deep industry insights on leveraging analytics for business success:
 * **From Data to Business Analytics:** Mr. Singh explained that while the journey may start with specific sectors like healthcare or energy analytics, it eventually culminates in **business analytics**. He emphasized that students should not just learn the tools but must develop an **"analytical mind"**.
 * **The industry-Academia Gap:** Addressing a common concern, he noted that MBA programs teach frameworks, while the industry focuses on **implementation and results.** He advised students to move beyond providing raw data and instead offer **outcomes, bullet points, and actionable notes** to management.
2952.title: Guest Lecture On Data Driven Operations For Business Excellence

2953.content:
## Interactive Session: Q&A Highlights

* **Strategic KPIs and Forecasting:** He stated that "if everything is important, nothing is important". KPIs should be goal-oriented, focusing on **Revenue, Margin, and Cost.** For survival in sectors like energy, accurate long-term forecasting is vital.
 * **Embracing Generative AI (GenAI):** Mr. Singh labelled GenAI as a "friend" that improves productivity. He cautioned that while humans are still needed for judgment, those who do not learn to work with AI will eventually be **replaced**.
 * **Operational Maturity:** He outlined a four-step model for business analysis:
2953.title: Guest Lecture On Data Driven Operations For Business Excellence

2954.content:
## Interactive Session: Q&A Highlights

**Descriptive:** What is happening?
**Diagnostic:** Why is it happening?
**Predictive:** What will happen next?
**Prescriptive:** What is the solution?
2954.title: Guest Lecture On Data Driven Operations For Business Excellence

2955.content:
## Career Guidance and Industry Readiness
Mr. Singh provided practical advice for students stepping into the professional world:
 * **Attitude Over Technical Skills:** He revealed that many companies now hire based on attitude, as technical skills can be taught.
 * **Ownership:** He redefined the role of a business analyst from a "job" to an **"ownership"** of the company’s success.
 * **Preparation:** He urged students to be **"company ready"** by researching a firm’s goals and demonstrating how they can add value (e.g., increasing a company’s worth from 1 million to 1.5 million) before an interview.
2955.title: Guest Lecture On Data Driven Operations For Business Excellence

2956.content:
## Ending of the Session
The session concluded with a note of high energy and gratitude. The student hosts, **Amrit and Mayra,** thanked Mr. Singh for bringing "textbook concepts to life". Gratitude was also extended to the faculty and the operations team for organizing the event. The lecture ended with a **group photograph** involving the guest, faculty, and students, marking the successful completion of the expert insight session
2956.title: Guest Lecture On Data Driven Operations For Business Excellence

#### Advancing Healthcare Education, Research, and Innovation
The School of Healthcare and Allied Sciences at GD Goenka University is a multidisciplinary center of excellence dedicated to advancing healthcare education, scientific discovery, and professional practice. Since its establishment in 2016, the School has evolved into one of India's leading destinations for healthcare and allied sciences education, attracting students from across India and several countries worldwide.

2972.content:

The School offers comprehensive education in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Physiotherapy, Public Health, Optometry, Clinical Research, Medical Laboratory Technology, Radiological Sciences, Cardiovascular Technology, Nursing, Clinical Embryology and other emerging healthcare disciplines. The Students benefit from a learner-centred pedagogical approach with international academic standards and professional competencies, integrating evidence-based practice, interdisciplinary learning, innovation, critical thinking, and ethical healthcare delivery.

### Report on Industrial Visit to National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL)

On 7th April 2026, M. Pharm. students from the Department of Pharmacy, School of Healthcare and Allied Sciences, participated in an industrial visit to the National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL) under the guidance of Dr. Rubina Bhutani and Dr. Sapna Joshi. The visit proved to be highly informative and enriching.
The session commenced with an interaction with the Director, Dr. P. L. Sahu, who provided valuable insights into the role of NDTL as India’s premier anti-doping laboratory. He highlighted its adherence to international standards and its contribution to ensuring fairness in sports through accurate detection of prohibited substances. He also emphasized the importance of ethics, discipline, and scientific precision.
3154.title: Report On Industrial Visit To National Dope Testing Laboratory Ndtl

3155.content:
### Report on Industrial Visit to National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL)

Students were then introduced to various laboratory sections, including sample receiving, quality management, and sample processing units. The Quality Management Section highlighted the importance of maintaining high standards through quality assurance and quality control practices in compliance with international guidelines, in the presence of Dr. Anandrajan T. Key techniques such as liquid-liquid extraction and enzymatic hydrolysis were demonstrated. Exposure to advanced instruments like GC-MS and LC-MS enhanced students’ understanding of modern analytical methods. The visit also included the biological section and EPO testing laboratory, where specialized procedures for doping analysis were explained.
Overall, the visit provided valuable practical exposure to advanced laboratory practices, quality systems, and regulatory frameworks, thereby strengthening students’ understanding of pharmaceutical and forensic applications.
3155.title: Report On Industrial Visit To National Dope Testing Laboratory Ndtl

3193.content:
### KRAMIERE- Embodied Image-Making Self & Story in Animation

**A Masterclass by Prof. Shilpa Ranade**
The Kremiere session at UID by Shilpa Ranade introduced students to animation as a storytelling medium deeply connected to literature, culture, and imagination. Mentored by Ram Mohan, she reflected on the evolution of animation in India and emphasized the importance of developing original narratives rooted in observation and cultural understanding.
Drawing inspiration from Eastern European animation and artists such as Yuri Norstein and Ishu Patel, she discussed how symbolism, folklore, music, and philosophy shape meaningful visual storytelling. She also highlighted the role of archetypes, literary influences, and material exploration through illustration, woodcut printing, and puppet-making in enriching animation practices.
3193.title: Kramiere  Embodied Image Making Self  Story In Animation

3194.content:
### KRAMIERE- Embodied Image-Making Self & Story in Animation

Through her experiences in filmmaking, illustration, and teaching, she encouraged students to look beyond software and focus on narrative depth, experimentation, textures, and cultural context. Overall, the session provided valuable insights into animation as an intellectually rich and emotionally engaging art form driven by storytelling integrity and creative exploration.
3194.title: Kramiere  Embodied Image Making Self  Story In Animation

3195.content:
### Thinking Beyond the Obvious

**A Masterclass by Anurag Sharma**
**Dated:** 23rd January 2026
**Venue:** UID Block, GD Goenka University
**Target Audience:** Students of B. Des (Hons) Visual Communication
**Faculty Coordinators:** Prof. Sumedha Garg, Asst. Prof. Devansh Sagar, Asst.Prof Pragya Jain & Asst.Prof Shrey Subodh.
As part of UID NCR’s commitment to industry-driven learning, a masterclass titled “Thinking Beyond the Obvious” was conducted on 23 January 2026 by UX design leader Anurag Sharma. The session encouraged students to move beyond aesthetics and focus on design as a problem-solving discipline rooted in empathy, inclusivity, and human-centred thinking. Through interactive discussions and exercises, students explored how questioning assumptions, understanding diverse user needs, and identifying real-world constraints are essential to effective design. A key highlight was the Curb-Cut Effect, demonstrating how designing for accessibility benefits a wider audience.
3195.title: Thinking Beyond The Obvious

3196.content:
### Thinking Beyond the Obvious

The session emphasised universal design as a mindset—one that considers diverse abilities and experiences from the outset rather than treating them as exceptions. Students were encouraged to think critically about everyday products and recognise how inclusive design can create meaningful, impactful solutions.
3196.title: Thinking Beyond The Obvious

3197.content:
### UID NCR at D-Arch Exhibition 2025

UID NCR proudly participated in the D-Arch Exhibition, held from 29 to 31 August 2025 at Pragati Maidan, New Delhi, presenting an inspiring showcase of creativity and innovation by UID NCR students.
The centrepiece of participation was three large-scale installations developed by Interior and Furniture Design and Product Design students. Each installation was conceived through an intensive design process—from research and conceptual sketches to prototype development—highlighting sustainable materials, context-sensitive solutions, and forward-looking architectural ideas.
To capture the event’s energy and document the making of these works, a dedicated media team provided behind-the-scenes and live coverage, allowing a wider audience to experience the students’ journey from studio to exhibition floor.
3197.title: Uid Ncr At D Arch Exhibition 2025

3198.content:
### UID NCR at D-Arch Exhibition 2025

This participation not only showcased the students’ design thinking and technical proficiency but also demonstrated UID NCR’s dedication to hands-on, experiential learning. By translating classroom concepts into full-scale installations, our students illustrated how academic exploration can evolve into innovative, real-world solutions for contemporary challenges.
3198.title: Uid Ncr At D Arch Exhibition 2025

3199.content:
###### 19 Aug, 2025
### World Humanitarian Day- 19 August 2025

The workshop focused on exploring a seamless travel journey through the lens of diverse user experiences. Product design students were divided into six groups, each assigned a specific persona: a wheelchair user, a person with blindness, a person with deafness, an individual with a neurodiverse disability, an older adult (85 years), and a mother with a pram. Guided by a suggested travel route—starting from living at home, getting out, using pavements, crossing roads, reaching a public transport station, boarding a transport vessel, and finally arriving and participating at the destination—each group discusses the challenges, needs, and inclusive solutions for their assigned persona. The session begins with an introduction, followed by group discussions and feedback, concluding with a summary. This workshop explores inclusive mobility aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goal 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities.
3199.title: World Humanitarian Day  19 August 2025

###### 18 Jul, 2025
### WORLD CRAFT FORUM 2024

Students of the Global Design programme, participated as volunteers at the prestigious event celebrating 60 years of the world craft council: titled ‘World Craft Forum 2024’ held in New Delhi. They were involved in setting up of stalls, guided tours and working with the international delegates and award winning artisans at the World Craft Forum.
There was a session on “Craft and the Creative Economy” at the World Craft Forum 2024, moderated by Director UID, Prof. Amrit Madan. The session had seven panelists representing India, US (North America), France, Kuwait, Ireland and UK. There were people working from grassroots to policy, from practice to creating craft ecologies, from cooperatives to startups. Topics revolving around entrepreneurship, authenticity, technology, micro-business, acceptance and more.
3200.title: World Craft Forum 2024

### Unsettled/Settled Humane Prototypes

The Interior and Furniture Design Area at UID NCR hosted a workshop on 'Unsettled/Settled Humane Prototypes' led by Amit Gupta, Niraja Adloori, and Shefali Shelat. The session delved into innovative design and prototyping concepts aimed at shaping a better future, encouraging participants to explore and create humane solutions to contemporary challenges. 3203.content:
### NEER: BEYOND THE SURFACE

**An Exhibition Display by the Semester-6 Students of Visual Communication**
This exhibition follows the course of the River Yamuna and its tributaries, the Hindon River and Sahibi River, as they move through the Delhi NCR region, bringing together fragments of water, memory, life, and shifting landscapes. Moving between presence and absence, flow and residue, the exhibition opens up a space to experience what gathers along the edges of a river.
Tracing these interconnected water bodies, NEER reflects on the ways rivers shape cities, communities, ecologies, and everyday life, while also carrying histories of neglect, transformation, and survival. Through layered narratives, textures, sounds, and visual traces, the exhibition invites viewers to look beyond the visible surface of water and engage with the hidden systems, memories, and relationships that continue to exist within and around these rivers.
3203.title: Neer Beyond The Surface

3204.content:
### NEER: BEYOND THE SURFACE

Rather than presenting the river as a fixed landscape, NEER approaches it as a living, changing entity, one that holds stories of movement, coexistence, loss, and renewal.
3204.title: Neer Beyond The Surface

3205.content:
### World Design Day

**Blended Experiences in Space – A Masterclass with Amardeep Behl**
**Can Interior Design Save the World? – A Masterclass with Madhav Raman**
On the occasion of World Design Day, the Interior & Furniture Design and Product Design departments hosted inspiring masterclasses by Amardeep Behl and Madhav Raman. The sessions explored how design can create meaningful human experiences through space, storytelling, sustainability, and cultural sensitivity.
Amardeep Behl shared how his studio, Design Habit, transforms architectural spaces into immersive environments through collaborations with artists and artisans across India. His lecture highlighted the importance of storytelling, materiality, and experiential design in shaping engaging spaces.
3205.title: World Design Day

3206.content:
### World Design Day

Madhav Raman focused on conservation, adaptive reuse, and context-driven design practices. He emphasized enhancing existing spaces while preserving their identity, emotion, and cultural value. Through his projects, students understood the importance of thoughtful interventions, local materials, and sustainable approaches in design.
Together, the lectures encouraged students to critically reflect on the relationship between design, people, culture, and the environment, inspiring more responsible and empathetic design practices.
3206.title: World Design Day

3207.content:
###### 15 Apr, 2026
### Interaction Session with Charuvi- Design Labs

Charuvi Design Labs conducted an industry internship session with us. The session provided valuable insights into the animation and game design industry, including current production pipelines, professional workflows, internship opportunities, and the skills required for working in studios.
The speakers also shared guidance on portfolio development, teamwork, creativity, and emerging technologies used in animation, VFX, gaming, and immersive media. The interaction was highly informative and motivating for students aspiring to build careers in the creative industry.
3207.title: Interaction Session With Charuvi  Design Labs

3208.content:
### Hair and Makeup Workshop

**A Workshop by Anjum Bhardwaj**
The Department of Fashion Design & Styling at UID NCR organized a two-day Hair and Makeup Workshop for Semester IV and VI students, conducted by renowned makeup artist and educator Anjum Bhardwaj. The workshop introduced students to the fundamentals of professional makeup artistry and its relationship with fashion styling, visual aesthetics, and presentation.
Students learned about skin analysis, product selection, occasion-based makeup, and techniques such as soft glam and full glam looks. Through live demonstrations and interactive sessions, they observed real-time makeup transformations customised to different face shapes, themes, and styling concepts.
3208.title: Hair And Makeup Workshop

3209.content:
### Hair and Makeup Workshop

The workshop also encouraged interdisciplinary learning, where students combined makeup with hairstyling, draping, accessorising, and garment styling to create complete visual narratives. Hands-on group activities allowed them to conceptualise and execute themed looks while developing teamwork, creative thinking, and styling coordination skills.
Overall, the workshop provided valuable industry exposure and helped students understand the connection between beauty, fashion, and visual storytelling through practical and collaborative learning experiences.
3209.title: Hair And Makeup Workshop

3210.content:
###### 25 Feb, 2026
### AANTRIK Designing Sublime Spatial Narratives of El Dorado

**A Masterclass with Arch. Anita Kulkarni and Arch. Yamini from Renu Art Foundation - 25th - 26th February, 2026**
The "Designing SUBLIME: Spatial Narratives of El Dorado" masterclass was conducted by Ar. Anita Kulkarni and Yamini from the Renu Art Foundation. As Architects and Spatial Designers, they introduced students to innovative perspectives on merging artistic concepts with spatial design. Participants explored personal resonances with the "El Dorado" show, using canvas and paint to artistically visualize their emotional and conceptual influences.
A key component of the workshop challenged students to redesign the stage for the production, tasking them with directing and modifying the narrative to reflect their unique viewpoints. This liberating exercise enabled students to cultivate abstract artistic expressions and successfully translate them into tangible design outcomes.
3210.title: Aantrik  Designing Sublime Spatial Narratives Of El Dorado

3211.content:
### IMPRINT- Visual Communication Conclave

**An Illustration Masterclass & Workshop by Bhavya Desai**
**Dated:** 19th – 20th February 2026
**Venue:** UID Block, GD Goenka University
**Target Audience:** Students of B. Des (Hons) Visual Communication
**Faculty Coordinators:** Prof. Sumedha Garg, Asst. Prof. Devansh Sagar, Asst.Prof Pragya Jain & Asst.Prof Shrey Subodh.
IMPRINT (formerly Drishticone+) marks a renewed chapter in visual dialogue at UID NCR, bringing together students, faculty, and industry professionals on a shared platform to bridge design education with real-world practice. Anchored in the pillars of Communication, Impact, and Community, the conclave fosters meaningful engagement through masterclasses, interactive sessions, and collaborative learning experiences led by leading designers and practitioners.
3211.title: Imprint  Visual Communication Conclave

3212.content:
### IMPRINT- Visual Communication Conclave

The session featuring illustrator and animator Bhavya Desai offered students valuable insights into building a sustainable creative career, emphasising clarity of intention, professional responsibility, and the importance of positioning in the design industry. Moving beyond conventional notions of style, the discussion highlighted how personal visual language evolves through observation, experience, and consistent practice.
Through hands-on activities and collaborative projects, students explored storytelling through observation, character-driven illustration, and real-world workflow simulations. A live digital illustration demonstration further enhanced understanding of process, technique, and execution in contemporary practice.
3212.title: Imprint  Visual Communication Conclave

3232.content:
### Centre of Conflict Resolution
A strong emphasis on alternative resolution mechanisms such as arbitration, mediation, and negotiation. It fosters a culture of constructive dialogue through hands-on training, simulated exercises, and community engagement. The Centre will facilitate dispute resolution through its Institutional Arbitration and Mediation Centre while also hosting workshops, international competitions, and policy discussions to equip students and professionals with practical skills.
Collaborations with organizations like the Indian Institute of Arbitration and Mediation (IIAM) enhances research opportunities and contributes to easing judicial backlogs. This initiative is instrumental in preparing a generation of legal professionals capable of handling complex disputes with empathy and efficiency.
3232.title: Center of Innovation Entrepreneurship

3233.content:
### Highlights
The Centre actively conducts research on mediation, arbitration, and negotiation, exploring their effectiveness in legal disputes and justice accessibility. It investigates early conflict detection strategies, community-based dispute resolution, and legal policy reforms at both national and international levels. Through capacity-building workshops and outreach initiatives, the Centre educates students, faculty, and the public on alternative dispute resolution methods.
It collaborates with legal institutions, policymakers, and NGOs to shape conflict resolution policies and peacebuilding efforts. Additionally, the Centre publishes research papers, reports, and case studies on emerging trends in dispute resolution. It integrates insights from law, psychology, sociology, and political science to develop comprehensive approaches and explores the role of digital platforms, AI, and virtual mediation tools in enhancing justice accessibility.

### Over the decades, automation has become a standardised production tool empowering manufacturers to gain better control of their operations and production processes. Bosch Rexroth India, one of the global market leaders in the area of Industrial Automation has recently entered into an MoU with GD Goenka University. Under this MoU, the University has established a Centre of Excellence in Industry 4.0 with products & technology supplied by Bosch Rexroth and this Centre of Excellence will be utilised for Training or Upskilling of the students, faculties & industry personnel on topics like PLCs, IIoT, SCADA & Industry 4.0.

# Centre of Indian Knowledge systems
> Centre of Indian Knowledge systems (CIKS) at GD Goenka University is dedicated to promoting and preserving India’s rich intellectual heritage.
The centre serves as a hub for interdisciplinary learning, integrating ancient wisdom with contemporary knowledge to address modern challenges. Through specialized courses, workshops, and research initiatives, the centre aims to foster intellectual inquiry, critical thinking, and a deeper appreciation of India's knowledge traditions.
3248.title: Centre of Indian Knowledge systems

3249.content:
## Vision
The vision of CIKS is to rejuvenate and mainstream Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) for the contemporary world in alignment with societal needs. The centre seeks to bridge the gap between traditional wisdom and modern disciplines, ensuring the relevance of IKS in today's academic and professional landscapes.
### Objectives
CIKS aligns with the objectives set by the UGC-IKS Division, Ministry of Education, Government of India, emphasizing:
 * Parampara – The continuous knowledge traditions of Bharata since time immemorial.
 * Drishti – Unique perspectives that make this knowledge system ‘Indian’ and valuable to the world.
 * Laukika Prayojana – Practical applications of IKS to solve contemporary and emerging global challenges.

The Centre serves as a vibrant platform for scholars, academicians, and industry experts to engage in interdisciplinary research and innovation across domains such as numismatics, digital assets, money and banking, cryptocurrencies, and emerging financial instruments.

3259.title: Currency Research Center

3260.content:
## Introduction to the Centre
The Centre aims to foster a robust academic ecosystem through awareness programmes, short-term certificate and diploma courses, and capacity-building initiatives focused on traditional and contemporary forms of money, including crypto assets, NFTs, and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs). With a forward-looking approach, the Centre is committed to undertaking consultancy projects and collaborative research in partnership with public institutions, financial bodies, and private stakeholders.
Through its diverse initiatives, the (Dr.) Rezwan Razack Centre aspires to become a national and global hub for thought leadership in currency studies, thereby contributing to informed policy, financial literacy, and academic excellence in the ever-evolving landscape of money and value.

### Recent Development in the Area of Digital Currency

Kazakhstan | — | Kazakhstan recently finished the piolet on CBDC has plans to launch the CBDC at the end of 2022.
France, Switzerland | Dec. 14, 2021 | France and Switzerland completed a test for the use of a wholesale CBDC for the cross-border transfers. It was popularly called as project Jura which was launched in June, 2021, along with the participation of the BIS (Bank of International Settlement) . The project was launched to check the effectiveness of ledger technology which facilitates the settlement. The banks explored the direct transfer of euro and Swiss franc wholesale CBDCs between Swiss and French commercial banks on a single distributed ledger technology platform operated by a third party, the BIS revealed in its press release.
3277.title: Currency Research Center

3278.content:
### Recent Development in the Area of Digital Currency

Brazil | Nov. 23, 2021 | The Central Bank of Brazil has a plan to launch the pilot for CBDC in 2022 and the final version of CBDC in 2024. On Dec. 8, 2021, the Brazil’s Chamber of Deputies (the lower house of the National Congress) approved Bill of Law 2303/15 (Projeto de Lei 2303/15) to regulate the virtual assets in Brazil. The bill defines the virtual assets “the digital representation of values that can be negotiated or transferred through electronic means.” (Projeto de Lei 2303/15, art. 3.). The bill excludes the digital representations of money or currency which are already regulated by law. The bill extensively provides for the regulation, supervision and punishment in case of breach.

#### Summary
Mewat is one of the district of Haryana where groundwater is used as one of the source for drinking, agriculture as well as for industrial purposes. Therefore, it was thought to investigate water quality of the Mewat district whether it is potable or not by physico-chemical analysis and further multivariate statistical methods will be used to facilitate the solution of environmental problems and suggest clues for the understanding of some natural processes.
The proposal will highlight the types of the pollutants present in the water samples collected from different areas and the factors affecting the concentration of each of the parameters. The finding will be helpful for the local government to plan the use and protection of groundwater resources.
The government can make sustainable strategies for management of water by various awareness & training programs to educate people regarding consequences of over exploitation of natural resources.

## About The Conference
Welcome to the International Conference 2021 “Beyond Academia: Exploring the Scope of Social Sciences” taking place on 16th July 2021 at GD Goenka University, India. The aim of the conference is to examine the key role that social sciences play in maintaining societal cohesion, stability and in articulating the dynamism of current times. The social sciences engage primarily with the study of society, social relationships and cultural change. As an academic field, they offer a wide range of perspectives that help to identify, articulate, examine and reflect on the dynamics of skills in demand in the current and predicted future economy.
3418.title: Conferences

3419.content:
## About The Conference

Yet, there seems to be a lacuna in understanding the value and the skill sets on offer by the social sciences. This is reflected to a large extent in the expectations and inquisitiveness on the part of young scholars, students and academicians alike, regarding the ‘future prospects’ of a ‘career in the social sciences’. Given this context, the Conference seeks to examine the capabilities, capacities and potential of the social sciences, to meet the demands of curricula, career and societal cohesion. This critical engagement, of social sciences and society, and social sciences from within, form the key thrust of the Conference.

##### The Impact Ranking
# Gender Equality
> By Focusing On Gender Equality
By Focusing On Gender Equality We not only adhere to the broader goal of promoting human rights but also address a fundamental issue that impedes social progress and sustainable development.
Promoting gender equality aligns closely with several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), such as SDG 5 - Gender Equality, which explicitly aims to end discrimination, violence, and harmful practices based on gender. Recognizing the significance of this goal, organizations worldwide are increasingly integrating gender equality initiatives into their projects and operations.
3426.title: Gender Equality

3427.content:
# Gender Equality

In many societies, gender inequality persists, limiting women #39;s access to education, economic opportunities, and decision-making roles. Addressing these disparities is a moral imperative and an economic and social necessity. When women are empowered and given equal opportunities, they contribute significantly to economic growth, innovation, and sustainable development.
3427.title: Gender Equality

3428.content:
# Gender Equality

Efforts to reduce gender inequality are multifaceted and include initiatives to close the gender pay gap, promote women #39;s leadership in various sectors, and eliminate discriminatory practices. By fostering an inclusive and diverse environment, organizations can tap into a broader range of talents, perspectives, and skills, ultimately driving innovation and success. Moreover, empowering women and ensuring their equal participation in decision-making processes contribute to more just and representative governance. In the long run, this can lead to the development of policies that address the entire population's needs, promoting social harmony and stability.
In science, politics, and business, a more gender-inclusive approach can result in breakthroughs and advancements that better address the needs of a diverse society. It is essential not only to create equal opportunities for women but also to challenge and change cultural norms and biases that perpetuate gender inequality.
3428.title: Gender Equality

3429.content:
# Gender Equality

As organizations increasingly recognize the interconnectedness of gender equality with broader societal goals, we can anticipate a more concerted effort to break down barriers, challenge stereotypes, and create a world where everyone, regardless of gender, can fully participate in and benefit from the fruits of development. In this way, the pursuit of gender equality becomes not just a project-specific focus but an integral part of a comprehensive strategy for sustainable and inclusive growth.

##### The Impact Ranking
# Clean Water Sanitation
GD Goenka University is strongly committed to promoting SDG 6 – Clean Water and Sanitation through sustainable infrastructure, research initiatives, and capacity-building activities that address water security and hygiene challenges.
The campus follows a regulated groundwater extraction system supported by a centralized RO plant, ensuring that all drinking water is treated and safe. Advanced UVF purification units and digital TDS meters are installed across hostels and academic buildings to ensure continuous monitoring and a high-quality water supply.
This infrastructure provides safe drinking water to over 2,000 students daily, reflecting the university’s commitment to responsible resource management. Beyond infrastructure, the university integrates sustainable practices by using purified water in hydroponics and polyhouse agriculture, enhancing water-use efficiency and promoting modern cultivation techniques.
3432.title: Clean Water Sanitation

3433.content:
# Clean Water Sanitation

Regular awareness programs on water conservation, sanitation, and hygiene are conducted for students and nearby communities, extending the university’s impact beyond campus.
Academically, GD Goenka University offers several courses directly aligned with SDG 6, including Environmental Studies, Water and Wastewater Management, Environmental Biotechnology, Soil and Water Conservation Engineering, Food Safety and Standards, Microbiology, Hydroponic Technology, and Sustainable Agriculture Systems. These courses equip students with scientific and practical knowledge to address water-related challenges and contribute to long-term sustainability. Through integrated infrastructure, academic engagement, and impactful research, GD Goenka University continues to lead by example in advancing SDG 6 at local and institutional levels.

##### The Impact Ranking
# Partnership For The Goals
> Sustainable Development Goal 17 (SDG 17)
Focuses on strengthening the means of implementation and revitalization of the Global Partnership for Sustainable Development. This goal recognizes that achieving sustainable development requires collective and coordinated efforts, collaboration, and the mobilization of resources at both national and international levels.
At its core, SDG 17 emphasizes the importance of partnerships and collaboration between governments, the private sector, civil society, and other stakeholders. The goal aims to foster a global environment that supports the achievement of all the other SDGs by promoting practical cooperation, coordination, and capacity-building.
3435.title: Partnership For The Goals

# Partnership For The Goals

One key aspect of SDG 17 is mobilizing financial resources for sustainable development. This involves encouraging domestic resource mobilization, attracting foreign direct investment, and providing financial assistance to developing countries. The goal recognizes the need for diverse and innovative financing mechanisms to support the implementation of sustainable development initiatives.
SDG 17 also focuses on enhancing technology transfer and promoting innovation. The goal aims to bridge the digital divide and ensure that technological advancements benefit all countries, particularly those in the developing world. By fostering innovation and supporting research and development, SDG 17 seeks to address global challenges and promote sustainable solutions.
3436.title: Partnership For The Goals

3437.content:
# Partnership For The Goals

The goal envisions a more open and inclusive global trading system. SDG 17 calls for reducing trade barriers, improving market access, and promoting fair and non-discriminatory trade practices. A well-functioning international trade system is crucial for economic growth, job creation, and poverty reduction. SDG 17 is closely linked with other sustainable development goals, as it provides the framework for the means of implementation necessary to achieve the broader agenda. It emphasizes the importance of partnerships (SDG 17) for the goals (SDGs 1-16), recognizing that collaborative efforts are essential for addressing complex and interconnected global challenges.

3491.content:
# Research

**Department actively participates in cutting edge research in national and international platforms and actively encourages students to support and participate in these research projects. Some major research projects include nuclear space propulsion, space tourism, remote sensing for disaster mitigation and CFD Analysis of Aeronautics Vehicles and Parts.**
Under the Supervision of [Dr. Ugur Guven](), advanced research into nuclear space propulsion techniques are being conducted. Dr Ugur Guven specialises in perfecting the Gaseous Core Rocket Engine for deep space missions. COMSOL and ANSYS software is used along with specially written FORTRAN code to calculate the Neutron interactions and fissile kinetics in propulsion and the corresponding fluid dynamics of the outward flow from the nozzle.
3491.title: Research

3492.content:
# Research

The Department is involved in using Computational Fluid Dynamics to analyse Aeronautical structures to see how they can be improved under various flow conditions. Students can also take part in this particular research under the supervision of their faculty. Also several CFD workshops are organized for interested students.
Department is currently involved in research for designing a Cubesat that will be deployed with a LEO orbit designed to provide maximum coverage on India, Indian Ocean and East Asia for the purpose of monitoring seismic activity and the corresponding electromagnetic activity in the upper atmosphere. Currently in 2025, the Department is starting its own Cubesat Project called QuakeSat to be completed by 2028 and launched by 2029.
3492.title: Research

Similar to the Expansion of Airports in 1930s that led to the Boom in Aviation Industry, now there is a large boom in Spaceports that is causing a large demand. [GD Goenka Aerospace Department]() is working on creating a blueprint for the Spaceports of the future as well as on [how to manage spaceports]() and will be publishing it as a book with the help of Aerospace students. Cutting edge research is conducted on this topic and presented regularly at international conferences.

### **Employment Opportunities Abroad****for Aerospace Engineers**
An Aerospace Engineer abroad can work as an aeronautical design engineer, flight engineer, aeronautical maintenance engineer, Aeronautical operations specialist, satellite design engineer, avionics engineer, flight systems design, rocket engineer, space systems engineer, space mission planner. In addition, many aerospace engineers work in the defense sector for defense companies and defense technologies such as missile systems, armed UAV, radar systems, intercept system. ### **Employment Opportunities in India for Aerospace Engineers**
India is one of the most prominent countries in aviation and astronautics. In the aviation sector, it is the third largest country after USA and China in terms of aviation flight traffic and its growing every day. In addition, India has its own indigenous aircraft and defense systems. On the space side, India is again the 3rd country in the world in terms of overall and deep space mission capability. India is at the forefront of space exploration and many startup companies are also coming up in India such as Skyroot and Bellatrix. Many Indian service companies such as TCS provide aerospace services to companies in Europe and USA. Hence, this is a great time to be an Indian in the global and national aerospace sector.

Students start to understand how contracts affect companies or how arguments are settled outside of courtrooms. Guest talks and workshops make things even more realistic. Hearing lawyers talking about their work in court or at companies makes things clearer in a way that can't be done with a textbook. Little by little, trust is earned. The move from college to work feels less scary and more normal after graduation.

3593.title: Blog

3594.content:
## Infrastructure and Learning Environment
Infrastructure is often a key element when students scan the list of [Law Colleges in Delhi NCR](). After all, learning works best in comfortable, focused, well-designed places. Modern classrooms with smart boards and interactive tools enhance debates, while silent digital libraries enable late-night study and inquisitive minds. Access to current publications and databases makes assignments interesting.
Moot courts provide a dimension. Entering these venues feels like entering a courtroom where confidence goes up with each argument. Learning spaces with technology allow simulations, presentations, and collaboration. Safe and student-friendly campuses matter more than brochures say. Clean hostels, safe neighborhoods, and friendly communal spaces foster belonging. Learning flows smoothly when students feel intellectually and personally encouraged, making law school productive, balanced, and rewarding.
3594.title: Blog

3595.content:
## Affordable Living and Student Lifestyle
Students are typically surprised by Gurgaon's manageability. Hostels, shared flats, and paying guest choices are cheaper than in downtown Delhi. That financial breathing room is extremely important. Students may study without stress. However, the lifestyle remains balanced. Long days in classrooms naturally lead to evenings with friends, coffee, or reading. Co-working spaces and libraries provide quiet locations for concentration, while cultural activities liven up daily life. Overall, Gurgaon is vibrant without being overpowering, making student life practical and fun.

## Concluding Remarks
The city of Gurgaon makes legal studies seem genuine with great academic institutions and regular professional experience. Nearby courts, firms, startups, and allied establishments quietly shape confident, practice-ready graduates.
[GD Goenka University's School of Law]() exemplifies heritage and current legal education in this environment. Under the GD Goenka legacy of academic quality, the School of Law combines rigorous study with practical applicability. Its programs teach legal comprehension and intelligent application. Moot courts, research culture, industry contact, and experienced teachers teach students to think critically, debate responsibly, and behave ethically. This strategy has earned the university credibility as the top Law Institute in Gurgaon.

Location is crucial, whether you want to work in corporate law, new technologies, policy, or global law. Professionally charged study spaces may discreetly boost confidence and clarity. Gurgaon, with GD Goenka University, offers that in full potential. Finally, matching your legal education with the correct location may launch a rewarding and promising legal career.

### Multi Commodity Exchange Workshop Report

**Multi Commodity Exchange Workshop Report**
**School of Management, August 12, 2022**
On August 12th, 2022, GD Goenka School of Management hosted a special Guest Lecture for MBAstudents of batch of 2022-2024. The lecture was delivered by Mr. Sanjay Gakhar, Vice President(Business Development) of Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd.
Mr. Sanjay Gakhar conducted an interactive session on what commodities are traded on the MCX, whythey are traded, how they are traded, and the history of those commodities on the consumer market.He also discussed how commodity prices are frequently changing in response to the supply and demand for these resources.
The School of Management student’s questions regarding the commodities market and commodityexchanges were clarified at the end of the session. The session was closed with a vote of thanks byProgram Head MBA & PGD Programs, Dr. Sudipta Sen Gupta.

Panel Discussion Report, School of ManagementAugust 10, 2022
On 10th August 2022, a panel discussion was organized by School of Management, GD GoenkaUniversity for MBA students of Batch 2022-2024.
The panel discussion was on Post Covid19 Career opportunities, it was taken up by leading recruiters and alumni of School of Management.
There were seven panelists and the first speaker was Mr. Vijay Tapo Kar, HR Head - Bata India Ltd.followed by second speaker Mr. Kallol Saha, Director HR - Crowne Plaza.

On 23 September 2025, School of Engineering and Sciences hosted an insightful guest lecture on ‘Experimental Approaches in Reinforced Concrete Structures: Recent Advancement’ conducted by Dr. Gaurav Sharma, Head of the Department, Lingaya’s Vidyapeeth and Postdoctoral Researcher at Incheon National University, South Korea. The session was attended by various students from the Department of Civil Engineering and Centre of Excellence in Occupational Health, Safety, Fire and Environment.
3683.title: Experimental Approaches In Reinforced Concrete Structures Recent Advancement

3684.content:
### Experimental Approaches in Reinforced Concrete Structures: Recent Advancement

The session majorly emphasized on integrating Acoustic Emission (AE) and Digital Image Correlation (DIC) for Synergistic Structural Health Monitoring of FRP Concrete Structures. Dr. Gaurav Sharma began with the growing use of Fibre Reinforced Polymer (FRP) materials in modern construction due to their high strength, durability, and corrosion resistance. He emphasized the challenges associated with monitoring FRP strengthened concrete structures using conventional inspection methods and the advanced non-destructive testing (NDT) techniques as a reliable alternative. The lecture also covered the concept of Acoustic Emission (AE), which enables real-time detection of internal damage such as crack initiation and fiber rupture, while Digital Image Correlation (DIC) provides full-field, high-resolution strain and displacement measurements on structural surfaces
3684.title: Experimental Approaches In Reinforced Concrete Structures Recent Advancement

3685.content:
### Experimental Approaches in Reinforced Concrete Structures: Recent Advancement

. The discussion on the synergistic integration of AE and DIC, offering a comprehensive and accurate approach to Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), left the participants with a deeper understanding of advanced diagnostic techniques and a strong appreciation for their practical relevance in modern structural analysis and monitoring applications.

### Visit to Institute of Pesticide Formulation Technology (IPFT), Gurugram

On 19 September 2025, the Department of Forensic Science organized an educational visit for UG and PG students to the Institute of Pesticide Formulation Technology (IPFT), Gurugram, an autonomous institution established in 1991 under the Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals, Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers, Government of India.
The visit began with an insightful session by Mr. Abhishek, Senior Scientist, who introduced the Biosciences Division and explained its work on bio-efficacy, phytotoxicity, phytotonicity, pesticide compatibility, and the impact of pesticides on beneficial organisms and the environment. This was followed by a detailed interaction with Ms. Nusrat Iqbal, Scientist, Formulation Division, who discussed the division’s consultancy services and highlighted its achievements in developing bio-botanical pesticide formulations as sustainable alternatives to synthetic pesticides.
3687.title: Visit To Institute Of Pesticide Formulation Technology Ipft Gurugram

3688.content:
### Visit to Institute of Pesticide Formulation Technology (IPFT), Gurugram

Students then engaged with Dr. Sudeep Mishra, Scientist, Analytical Division, who elaborated on the division’s role in quality control, residue analysis, method development, and the use of advanced analytical instruments. The visit concluded with an address by Dr. Samsul Alam, Director, who emphasized IPFT’s commitment to innovative research, eco-friendly technologies, and industry support. Students also explored instruments such as GC-MS, LC-MS, HPLC, and FTIR, gaining valuable hands-on exposure that strengthened their understanding of real-world pesticide research and analytical techniques.
The visit was well organized by Ms. Mala Bharti, Assistant Professor and Mr. Fakhruddin Ahmed, Assistant Professor.

### 10th Convocation of GD Goenka University 2024

The 10th Convocation of GD Goenka University was held today at the iconic Manekshaw Centre, Delhi, celebrating the achievements of 1491 graduates.
The event was graced by esteemed dignitaries, including the Chief Guest, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Hon'ble Minister of Culture & Tourism, Government of India, and the Guest of Honour, Gen VK Singh (Retd.), Former Chief of the Army Staff and Former Minister of State in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and Ministry of Civil Aviation, who delivered inspiring addresses that ignited aspirations and celebrated excellence.
The ceremony commenced with the academic procession, led by the Chief Guest, Guest of Honour, Chancellor Mrs. Renu Goenka, Vice Chairperson, GD Goenka Group, Pro-Chancellor, Mr. Nipun Goenka, Managing Director, GD Goenka Group, and Vice Chancellor, Prof. (Dr.) Kim Menezes.

### WEBINAR ON "Recent Developments in Mechanical Engineering” 30 July 2020 at 11:00 AM

Dr.Vinay Vakharia completed his Ph.D. from IIITDM Jabalpur in 2015 in the area of Fault diagnosis. He has applied Signal Processing techniques such as wavelets and artificial intelligence techniques to diagnose various bearing faults. He highlighted Machine Learning and its Application for vibration analysis. He elaborated about the Machine Learning application used with artificial Intelligence techniques, key indicators and the subsequent need of signal and image processing involved in the study. He also discussed the vibration analysis about these criterions.
Dr. Jatin Patel, Associate Professor, PDEU University, Gujrat presented a detailed presentation on research projects completed by their students. He highlighted the solar and refrigeration system. He also discussed the renewable energy for desalination and water treatment processes and their development with the help of software tools.

3840.content:
## Frequently Asked Questions
What programs does the School of Psychology offer?
### The School of Psychology offers:
##### Undergraduate Programs
 * B.A. (Hons.) Psychology
 * B.Sc. (Hons.) Clinical Psychology (RCI-approved)

##### Postgraduate Programs
 * M.A. Psychology
 * M.A. Clinical Psychology (RCI-approved)

##### Diploma Programs
 * Post Graduate Diploma in Clinical Psychology (RCI-approved)
 * Doctoral Program: Ph.D. in Psychology

What is special about the B.Sc. (Hons.) Clinical Psychology program?
3840.title: Faq

3841.content:
### The B.Sc. (Hons.) Clinical Psychology program is RCI-approved and designed to give students a strong foundation in:
 * Clinical assessment and psychodiagnostics
 * Basic counseling and psychotherapeutic skills
 * Mental health and rehabilitation

It is ideal for students who want to build a career in clinical settings and later pursue M.A./M.Sc. Clinical Psychology or M.Phil. in Clinical Psychology
What are the eligibility criteria for the M.A./M.Sc. Clinical Psychology program?
3841.title: Faq

3842.content:
### To apply, candidates must have:
 * A Bachelor's degree in Psychology or a closely related field (minimum 55% aggregate)
 * Preferably studied courses in Abnormal Psychology, Counseling, and Research Methods at the undergraduate level

Admission may also involve an entrance test and personal interview to assess aptitude for clinical training
Does completing M.A./M.Sc. Clinical Psychology make me eligible for RCI registration?
Yes, the M.A./M.Sc. Clinical Psychology program is RCI-approved. After completion, students can apply for RCI registration as Clinical Psychologists once they also complete the mandatory M.Phil. Clinical Psychology or Psy.D. (Doctor of Psychology) from an RCIapproved institute.
What is the Post Graduate Diploma in Counseling and Psychotherapy?
3842.title: Faq

3843.content:
### This is a one-year RCI-approved diploma designed to train graduates and working professionals in:
 * Counseling skills
 * Psychotherapeutic techniques
 * Ethics and professional practice

Graduates can work in schools, NGOs, community centers, and mental health support programs as qualified counselors
What kind of practical exposure is included in RCI-approved programs?
### All RCI-approved programs emphasize hands-on training, including:
 * Supervised practice sessions in counseling and therapy
 * Case study analysis
 * Fieldwork in hospitals, schools, and NGOs
 * Clinical internship under qualified supervisors

Do students get supervised clinical training?
3843.title: Faq

3844.content:
### Yes. Clinical supervision is a crucial part of training. Students work with licensed Clinical Psychologists during:
 * Psychodiagnostic assessments
 * Counseling sessions
 * Therapeutic interventions

This ensures they meet the RCI’s required clinical hours for eligibility.
Are research projects mandatory for Clinical Psychology students?
Yes. Students must complete a dissertation/research project in their final year, guided by faculty members. This research experience strengthens their understanding of evidencebased practice and prepares them for higher studies like M.Phil. or Ph.D.
What is the career scope after completing an RCI-approved program?
3844.title: Faq

3845.content:
### Career opportunities include:
 * Clinical Psychologist (with M.Phil./Psy.D. + RCI registration)
 * Counselor in schools, NGOs, and rehabilitation centers
 * Psychometrician and assessment specialist
 * Research associate or faculty member in universities
 * Mental health consultant for corporates or wellness programs

How do these programs compare with non-RCI psychology programs?
### RCI-approved programs are recognized for professional practice, which means:
 * You can legally provide clinical services
 * You become eligible for government jobs and licensed practice
 * You can register with the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI), which is mandatory for Clinical Psychologists in India
3845.title: Faq

### Departmental Seminar Series -SoES

School of Engineering & Sciences (SoES), GD Goenka University organized a Departmental Seminar Series on 28 July 2022. Ms. Vinita Makkar, a research scholar in Mathematics, under the supervision of Prof. (Dr.) Naresh Sharma, has delivered a talk on ‘A Mathematical Modelling of Magnetohydrodynamic Nanofluid Flow Induced by Three Dimensional Stretching Surface’.
In this webinar, she detailed about the non-Newtonian nanofluids in relation to magnetohydrodynamic flow and free stream velocity over three-dimensional stretching sheet. She discussed about parametric analysis involving velocity, temperature, concentration and also about continuity, momentum and energy which involved ordinary differential equations and Runge Kutta Fehlber procedure. She highlighted various applications in different domains of manufacturing, industry and medicine.

**PARTICIPATION IN “ROKO THALASSEMIA” RALLY** “Treatment without prevention is simply unsustainable” Physiotherapy students from SoMAS, GD Goenka University, participated in “Roko Thalassemia” seminar and awareness Rally organised by Artemis Hospitals in association with Mahavir International and Indian Red Cross Society, Gurugram, on January 7, 2018. More than 250 bikers joined the campaign to spread awareness about the disease. Expressing concern over the growing number of thalassemia patients, Dr. Gaurav Kharya, Senior Consultant and Head Paediatric Hemato-oncology and bone marrow transplant at Artemis Hospital, urged the youth to check their thalassemia status before getting married or planning children. A free thalassemia (HbA2) camp was also conducted on this occasion.
