3951.content:
### The Centre for Conflict Resolution

The Centre for Conflict Resolution (CCR) is committed to transforming how disputes are addressed, with a strong emphasis on alternative resolution mechanisms such as arbitration, mediation, and negotiation. It fosters a culture of constructive dialogue through hands-on training, simulated exercises, and community engagement. The Centre will facilitate dispute resolution through its Institutional Arbitration and Mediation Centre while also hosting workshops, international competitions, and policy discussions to equip students and professionals with practical skills. Collaborations with organizations like the Indian Institute of Arbitration and Mediation (IIAM) enhance research opportunities and contribute to easing judicial backlogs. This initiative is instrumental in preparing a generation of legal professionals capable of handling complex disputes with empathy and efficiency.
3951.title: About

3952.content:
#### Objective of the Centre
 * Equip students with knowledge and practical skills in mediation, arbitration, and negotiation as effective alternatives to litigation.
 * Conduct research on conflict resolution mechanisms, legal frameworks, and policy recommendations for improvement of justice delivery system.
 * Offer students hands-on experience through simulated exercises, and resolution of real-life cases.
 * Engage in community outreach programs, advocacy, and awareness campaigns to promote peaceful dispute resolution and advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
 * Collaborate with legal practitioners, government institutions, and international organizations to enhance knowledge exchange and career opportunities in conflict resolution.

* Research
 * Extension Activities
 * Allied Activities
3952.title: About

3953.content:
## Research
### Highlights
#### Research
 * Conducting empirical research to investigate the effectiveness of mediation, arbitration, and negotiation in resolving legal disputes and enhancing access to justice.
 * Analyzing strategies for early conflict detection, community-based dispute resolution, and sustainable peace initiatives.
 * Examining national and international laws, judicial interventions, and policy reforms that impact dispute resolution and justice delivery.

## Extension Activities
### Highlights
#### Extension Activities
 * Organizing capacity-building workshops for students and faculty on effective conflict resolution techniques.
 * Conducting outreach programs to educate the public on alternative dispute resolution (ADR) methods and access to justice.
 * Collaborating with legal institutions, policymakers, and non-governmental organizations to develop conflict resolution policies and implement peacebuilding initiatives.
3953.title: About

3954.content:
### Highlights
#### Allied Activities
 * Publishing research papers, reports, and case studies on emerging trends and best practices in conflict resolution.
 * Conducting collaborative studies integrating law, psychology, sociology, political science, and other disciplines to develop holistic approaches to conflict resolution.
 * Exploring digital platforms, AI, and virtual mediation tools to improve access to justice and efficiency in dispute resolution.

#### Mission
 * To foster a society where conflicts are resolved through dialogue, fairness, and innovative legal approaches, shaping a more just and harmonious world.
 * To lead in legal education and research on dispute resolution, advancing alternative mechanisms that enhance access to justice and sustainable peace.
 * To cultivate a culture of effective conflict management by bridging theory and practice, preparing legal experts to address disputes with professionalism and integrity.
3954.title: About

3955.content:
#### Vision
To be a centre of excellence in conflict resolution, fostering a culture of peaceful dispute settlement through legal research, practical training, and community engagement.
3955.title: About

3956.content:
### Head of Centre’s Message
> The Indian judicial system has been actively seeking a feasible conflict resolution mechanism to reduce the mammoth pendency of cases in courts.
The objective of conflict resolution is to achieve a mutually agreeable settlement that meets the satisfaction of all parties concerned, without resorting to formal court proceedings, thereby creating a win-win situation for both the parties. The aim of the Centre for Conflict Resolution (CCR), established by School of Law, GD Goenka University is the advancement of research, scholarship, education and training in the fields of arbitration, mediation and negotiation. The CCR represents a collaborative effort by the School of Law GD Goenka University and Indian Institute of Arbitration and Mediation (IIAM). The Centre aspires to cultivate a generation of legal practitioners who prioritize harmony, empathy, and innovative problem-solving in their approach to conflict resolution.
##### Dr. Apoorva Dixit

### The Centre for IP Studies, Research and Extension

The Centre for IP Studies, Research and Extension is a pioneering hub for innovation, education, and the commercialization of intellectual property. It focuses on creating a robust ecosystem for IP management, offering training programmes for scientists, researchers, and legal professionals. Its key activities include establishing IP facilitation cells, developing incubation centres, and supporting start-ups with patent filings and portfolio management. Through seminars, diploma programmes, and collaborative workshops, the Centre enhances IP awareness and skill development across various sectors. By partnering with institutions and corporations, it plays a pivotal role in shaping IP policy, fostering economic growth, and contributing to India’s global competitiveness in innovation.
 * Research
 * Extension Activities
 * Allied Activities

3962.content:
## Research
### Highlights
#### Research
The Centre conducts research on various aspects of intellectual property, including:
 * The effectiveness of patent laws and their impact on innovation and technological growth.
 * Legal challenges in digital copyright and evolving media landscapes.
 * The role of trademarks in branding, commercial success, and consumer protection.
 * Strategies to integrate IP enforcement with competition law and policy.
 * The intersection of emerging technologies such as AI, blockchain, and biotechnology with IP law.

## Extension Activities
### Highlights
#### Extension Activities
The Centre actively promotes IP awareness and knowledge sharing through:
 * Capacity-building workshops for students, faculty, and industry professionals.
 * Public outreach programmes on the significance of intellectual property rights.
 * Collaborations with policymakers, legal institutions, and industries to develop effective IP policies.

 * Promoting IP awareness and capacity building through dynamic training programmes, workshops, and academic initiatives.
 * Supporting innovators, start-ups, and legal professionals with comprehensive IP facilitation, incubation, and portfolio management services.

 * Cultivating strategic collaborations with academic institutions, industry, and government bodies to strengthen India’s innovation ecosystem.

The Centre’s comprehensive approach includes developing specialised academic programs, hosting conferences, providing consultancy services, and publishing influential research. By fostering partnerships with global organizations, the Centre aims to shape innovative policies and practical solutions that align with sustainable development goals. This initiative not only equips future legal professionals with a strong foundation in environmental law but also influences governance practices worldwide.

4005.content:
### The Centre for Constitutional Law and Human Rights

The Centre for Constitutional and Human Rights Law (CCHRL) stands as a dynamic and pioneering institution dedicated to research, education, and advocacy in the fields of constitutional and human rights law. In an era defined by rapid societal transformations—fueled by technological innovation, globalization, environmental shifts, and evolving social movements—the Centre is committed to understanding and addressing the profound impacts these changes have on jurisprudence and governance.
4005.title: About

4006.content:
### The Centre for Constitutional Law and Human Rights

CCHRL adopts a multidisciplinary approach, integrating insights from law, public policy, technology, and environmental sciences to generate innovative legal solutions and promote sustainable governance. Aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the Centre's initiatives aim to strengthen constitutional democracies, advance the protection of human rights, and equip societies with the tools necessary to navigate the complexities of a rapidly changing world. Through cutting-edge research, capacity-building programs, policy advocacy, and global collaborations, the Centre aspires to shape informed policymaking, foster robust constitutional frameworks, and empower stakeholders—including academics, policymakers, and legal practitioners—to champion the cause of justice and equity on a global scale
4006.title: About

4007.content:
### The Centre for Constitutional Law and Human Rights

. CCHRL endeavors to serve as a beacon for transformative legal thought and action, addressing the pressing challenges of our time with a forward-thinking and inclusive vision.
4007.title: About

4008.content:
### Highlights
#### Governance and Advisory Board:
The governance structure of the Centre ensures strategic direction and accountability. A Centre Head with expertise in constitutional and human rights law leads the Centre, supported by internal members engaged in interdisciplinary research. An advisory board comprising constitutional scholars, human rights experts, judges, and former government officials provides guidance on ensuring the relevance and impact of the Centre's work. This robust governance framework enables the Centre to achieve its mission effectively and sustainably.
4008.title: About

4009.content:
#### Research and Analysis:
The Centre prioritizes investigating the societal variables that drive changes in constitutional and human rights law. Key focus areas include understanding the influence of technological advancements on legal systems, the effects of globalization on constitutional norms and governance, and the role of social movements in shaping human rights advocacy. Furthermore, the Centre explores how environmental and demographic shifts reshape legal frameworks, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving interplay between society and law.
4009.title: About

4010.content:
#### Education and Training:
Education and capacity-building are central to the Centre's mission. The Centre develops and delivers workshops, courses, and training programs tailored to address emerging challenges in constitutional law and human rights. Special attention is given to critical topics such as digital rights, climate justice, transnational governance, and their implications for jurisprudence. These programs are designed to equip students, researchers, and professionals with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate complex legal issues effectively.
4010.title: About

4011.content:
#### Policy Advocacy:
The Centre plays an active role in drafting evidence-based policy recommendations to address contemporary challenges in constitutional and human rights law. These include the impact of new technologies, the dynamics of shifting political landscapes, and the influence of social movements. By providing actionable insights, the Centre empowers legal systems to adapt to rapid societal changes while ensuring that constitutional principles remain intact and robust.
4011.title: About

4012.content:
#### Global Networking and Collaboration:
Recognizing the importance of collaboration, the Centre engages with a diverse range of stakeholders, including experts in human rights, governance, technology, and law. Partnerships are built with academic institutions, international organizations, policymakers, and civil society groups to foster a holistic approach to constitutional and human rights law. These collaborations aim to create a global platform for sharing knowledge, addressing constitutional reforms, and promoting innovative legal solutions.
4012.title: About

4013.content:
#### Annual Symposiums and Conferences:
The Centre organizes flagship events that address cutting-edge issues in constitutional and human rights law. Topics such as the legal implications of artificial intelligence and surveillance technologies, constitutional responses to migration and urbanization, and comparative analyses of social justice movements are explored. These symposiums and conferences bring together scholars, policymakers, and practitioners to deliberate on pressing challenges and share actionable insights.
4013.title: About

4014.content:
#### Publications:
The Centre contributes to scholarly discourse through thematic publications that address the intersection of constitutional law with technological and environmental challenges. Case studies on evolving human rights norms across jurisdictions provide critical analyses of global trends. Additionally, the Centre supports semi/fully funded conferences, colloquiums, and events that facilitate knowledge dissemination and collaboration. Research outputs are aimed at influencing policy decisions and fostering academic excellence.
4014.title: About

4015.content:
#### Fellowships and Visiting Scholars Program:
To encourage interdisciplinary approaches, the Centre invites experts in fields such as constitutional law, human rights, technology, AI, and environmental sciences. The Fellowships and Visiting Scholars Program promotes collaborative legal research, fostering an exchange of ideas and insights. These initiatives aim to build a diverse and dynamic community of scholars committed to addressing the complex challenges of constitutional and human rights law.
4015.title: About

4016.content:
#### Workshops and Capacity-Building Programs:
The Centre organizes workshops and capacity-building initiatives to train legal professionals on adaptive strategies for emerging legal challenges. Emphasis is placed on equipping participants with practical skills and tools to address rapid changes in jurisprudence. These programs bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application, empowering stakeholders to contribute effectively to constitutional governance and human rights advocacy.
4016.title: About

4017.content:
#### Institutional Partnerships:
Institutional collaborations form the backbone of the Centre's activities. By partnering with universities and research institutions specializing in constitutional and human rights law, the Centre aims to address societal changes proactively. These collaborations focus on developing policy recommendations to mitigate the potential negative consequences of social changes while maximizing positive outcomes. Engagements with policymakers and civil society organizations further strengthen the Centre’s impact.
4017.title: About

4018.content:
#### Governance and Advisory Board:
The governance structure of the Centre ensures strategic direction and accountability. A Centre Head with expertise in constitutional and human rights law leads the Centre, supported by internal members engaged in interdisciplinary research. An advisory board comprising constitutional scholars, human rights experts, judges, and former government officials provides guidance on ensuring the relevance and impact of the Centre's work. This robust governance framework enables the Centre to achieve its mission effectively and sustainably.
4018.title: About

4019.content:
#### Research and Analysis:
The Centre prioritizes investigating the societal variables that drive changes in constitutional and human rights law. Key focus areas include understanding the influence of technological advancements on legal systems, the effects of globalization on constitutional norms and governance, and the role of social movements in shaping human rights advocacy. Furthermore, the Centre explores how environmental and demographic shifts reshape legal frameworks, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving interplay between society and law.
#### Mission
To conduct multidisciplinary and comparative research, educate stakeholders, and influence public policy through evidence-based recommendations, addressing the evolving interplay of societal variables—such as technology, globalization, human rights, and political shifts—that impact constitutional and human rights law.
4019.title: About

4020.content:
#### Vision
To understand and address the dynamic changes and challenges in contemporary jurisprudence, with a focus on constitutional, comparative constitutional law, and human rights law. By analyzing the rapid evolution of legal systems and societal norms, the Centre seeks to foster informed policymaking and advocacy for robust constitutional democracies and the protection of human rights globally.
4020.title: About

> “At the heart of the Centre for Constitutional and Human Rights Law lies a commitment to addressing the pressing challenges of our time through innovative research, education, and advocacy. In an era of rapid societal transformation, constitutional principles and human rights face unprecedented opportunities and challenges.

4022.content:

Your support and collaboration will enable us to build a future that is just, equitable, and sustainable for all.”

#### School of Management
### General Management Area

This area primarily encompasses two key specializations: Entrepreneurship and International Business, along with foundational courses in communication and law. Each of these components is vital in shaping well-rounded professionals who can effectively navigate the complexities of today’s business environment. The objective of this specialization is to equip students with essential skills and knowledge of the global marketplace, preparing them for successful careers and enabling them to excel in diverse and dynamic settings.
4102.title: About

4103.content:
### Message from the Head of Department
> Welcome to the Department of General Management Area at GD Goenka University!
The General Management area builds a strong foundation for navigating the complexities of entrepreneurship and international business. It blends critical thinking, strategic insight, and global awareness to prepare professionals who can adapt and excel in diverse environments.
Through platforms like the E Cell and IB Club, students engage in debates, innovation forums, and interactions with industry experts, translating classroom learning into real opportunities.
With over sixteen years of academic and industry exposure, I encourage an approach rooted in curiosity and initiative—qualities that open doors to lasting impact in the business world.
##### Dr. Neetu Ahmed
Area Chair – General Management

4104.content:
## Students club and Societies
### Highlights
#### Students club and Societies
**E-Cell:** To cultivate students’ entrepreneurial spirit and harness their potential for innovative, forward-thinking ideas, we offer mentorship and support. This is accomplished through speaker sessions with industry leaders, workshops, and events like Innospark, Udyami Bazar designed to foster entrepreneurship and encourage students to share ideas that contribute to growth and development.
**IB Club:** The IB club activities are planned and carried out by student coordinators with guidance from the relevant faculty members. A wide range of events, including seminars, debates, quizzes, are regularly organized to develop the essential skills needed for success in the corporate world. The club hosts industry experts for guest talks and seminars. The IB Club invites students from all majors to engage in discussions about business and economic issues at both local and international levels.

4127.content:
### Human Resource Management Area

The Human Resource (HR) specialization in MBA programs equips students with the knowledge and skills required to manage and develop human capital effectively within organizations. It covers key areas such as human resource management, Human Resource Planning, recruitment and selection, performance management, compensation, employee engagement, Industrial Relations and labor laws, Emotional Intelligence, Training and Development,Human Resource Metrics and Analytics, Talent management.Overall Students learn how to align HR strategies with business goals to foster productivity and ensure workforce well-being. The curriculum often emphasizes practical approaches through case studies, internships, role-playing exercises, guest lectures, Industrial Visit, all of this to help students gain real-world experience. With the rise of digital transformation, HR courses also explore contemporary topics like HR analytics, talent management systems and the role of AI in enhancing HR operations.

4128.content:
### Message from the Head of Department
> Welcome to the Department of Human Resource Management Area at GD Goenka University!
The Human Resource area warmly welcomes the new MBA cohort. This specialization is committed to developing professionals who understand how people drive organizational success. The curriculum blends foundational HR principles with contemporary topics such as HR analytics, talent management systems, and the impact of digital transformation on workplaces. Supported by initiatives like The Trailblazers Society, students gain exposure through industry visits, guest sessions, and events such as the annual HR Summit. With extensive academic and industry experience, I encourage every student to explore, engage, and evolve into impactful leaders of tomorrow.

## Students club and societies
### Highlights
#### Students club and societies
The Trailblazers Society, a student-driven HR club, is dedicated to enhancing students' knowledge and skills in the fields of Human Resource Management, organizational behavior, and leadership development. The club offers a dynamic platform for students to engage with HR industry professionals through guest lectures, gain practical insights through industry visits, and actively participate in events such as the HR Summit, featuring panel discussions with corporate leaders. Through initiatives like the Corporate Walk Show and interactive workshops, the club aims to equip students with essential HR and managerial competencies, fostering a community passionate about driving organizational success and shaping the future of leaders.

4159.content:
#### School of Management
### Finance Area

The Finance Department at School of Management , GD Goenka University, offers foundational and specialised courses in Accounting and Finance. The students are offered a holistic view of the financial system encompassing Institutions, Markets, Services and Regulations. The finance courses,designed in alignment with industry requirements, cover areas in Accounting, Management Accounting, Investment and Portfolio Management, International Finance, Corporate Financial Management, Wealth Management ,Corporate Valuation and Risk Management. Interactive classroom sessions and experiential learning methods like stock simulations, financial modelling and case studies makes the learning holistic and skill based.
4159.title: About

4160.content:
### Message from the Head of Department
> Welcome to the Department of Finance at GD Goenka University!
Finance is the language of business, shaping decisions that drive growth and innovation. At the School of Management, the Finance Department combines academic rigor with hands on learning—stock market simulations, financial modelling workshops, and industry interactions—to cultivate analytical minds and confident decision makers.
The Finance Club further enriches this journey by fostering curiosity about markets, trends, and emerging opportunities.With experience spanning both academia and the financial services sector, my focus remains on nurturing professionals who approach challenges with clarity, integrity, and strategic insight.
##### Dr. Sunrita Chaudhuri
Area Chair-Finance

4293.content:
### Department of Physiotherapy

The Physiotherapy Department at GD Goenka University is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities that enhance the learning experience and support comprehensive clinical training. Our specialised laboratories are designed to provide students with hands-on experience in various aspects of physiotherapy practice. The following labs are integral to our program:
 * **Electrotherapy Lab:** The laboratory is equipped with advanced electrotherapy and rehabilitation modalities, including Ultrasound, TENS, IFT, LASER Therapy, Curapod, Microwave Diathermy, Infrared Radiation, Upper and Lower Limb CPM Units, Traction Units, Whirlpool Bath, Contrast Bath, and Paraffin Wax Therapy. It provides students with hands-on training in pain management, rehabilitation, tissue healing, and functional recovery.
4293.title: Facilities

4294.content:
### Department of Physiotherapy

* **Exercise Therapy Lab:** Focused on therapeutic exercises, this lab features a variety of equipment and tools that facilitate rehabilitation and conditioning. Students gain practical knowledge in designing and implementing exercise programs for patients with different conditions.
 * **Biomechanics Lab:** This lab provides a platform for studying human movement and mechanics. Equipped with motion analysis systems and force platforms, it allows students to analyse gait, posture, and other biomechanical aspects critical to physiotherapy practice.
 * **Neurology Lab:** Designed to focus on neurological conditions, this lab features equipment and resources to assess and treat patients with neurological impairments. Students learn to apply specific techniques to improve motor function and coordination.
4294.title: Facilities

4295.content:
### Department of Physiotherapy

* **Orthopaedics Lab:** This lab simulates a clinical environment for orthopaedic assessments and treatments. Students practise techniques related to joint mobilisation, manual therapy, and rehabilitation strategies for musculoskeletal injuries.
 * **Functional Diagnostic Lab:** This lab is equipped with tools to evaluate functional capacity and performance. Students learn to conduct assessments that help in developing personalised treatment plans based on patients' functional abilities.
 * **Exercise Tolerance Lab:** Focused on cardiovascular health, this lab features equipment for conducting exercise tolerance tests. Students gain experience in evaluating patients’ cardiovascular fitness and designing appropriate exercise regimens.
4295.title: Facilities

4296.content:

##### Research Facilities
Access to resources for conducting research, including specialized equipment and software for data analysis, enabling students and faculty to engage in innovative research projects.
##### Library Resources
A comprehensive collection of books, journals, and digital resources specific to physiotherapy and allied health sciences, supporting both academic learning and research.

On-campus facilities for conducting rehabilitation programs, providing students with opportunities to engage with patients and apply their learning in real-world settings.

**Empowering Zoomers to Code the Future:**
The **Department of Nursing** is the heartbeat of our institution, dedicated to transforming aspiring students into compassionate, highly skilled healthcare leaders. We blend rigorous academic theory with intensive clinical practice to ensure our graduates meet the evolving demands of modern medicine.
Our department prides itself on a curriculum that emphasizes **patient-centered care** , ethical practice, and evidence-based research. With access to advanced simulation labs and diverse clinical rotations, students gain the hands-on experience necessary to excel in high-pressure environments.
Driven by a mission to improve community health, we foster an environment of lifelong learning and professional growth. Whether in the classroom or at the bedside, our faculty is committed to nurturing the next generation of nursing professionals who will lead with both **competence and heart**.

4308.content:
### Department of Nursing

Research is the cornerstone of professional nursing practice. Our department is dedicated to bridging the gap between theoretical knowledge and clinical application, ensuring that patient care is always guided by the latest scientific evidence.
#### Our Research Focus Areas
**We encourage faculty and students to explore diverse domains, including:**
 * **Clinical Excellence:** Improving patient outcomes in critical care, oncology, and geriatrics.
 * **Nursing Education:** Developing innovative teaching methodologies and simulation-based learning.
 * **Community Health:** Investigating public health trends and preventive care in rural and urban settings.
 * **Healthcare Policy:** Analysing the impact of nursing leadership on healthcare delivery systems.
4308.title: Research

4309.content:
#### Research Resources
 * **Institutional Review Board (IRB):** A dedicated ethics committee to oversee and guide all nursing research projects.
 * **Collaborative Partnerships:** Opportunities to work alongside multidisciplinary teams in medicine, pharmacy, and public health.
 * **Digital Library:** Access to international journals such as The Lancet, Journal of Advanced Nursing, and PubMed.

#### Student Involvement
**We believe in nurturing an inquisitive mind from the start. Our students participate in:**
 * **Undergraduate Projects:** Learning the basics of data collection and literature review. Conducting original research under the mentorship of experienced faculty.

**Research in nursing is not just about data; it is about finding better ways to care, heal, and lead.**

The Area of Interior and Furniture Design at UID is committed to transforming spaces and creating meaningful design experiences that extend beyond traditional boundaries and crafting bespoke furniture that merges innovation with artistry. This area immerses students in the intricate blend of art and science within interior design, emphasizing the creation of spaces that are not only visually compelling but also intelligent, sustainable, and attuned to human needs. By merging functionality with aesthetic appeal and prioritizing environmentally conscious solutions, the area equips students to craft spaces that deeply connect with their inhabitants.
4377.title: About

4378.content:
### Department of Interior Architecture & Design

Working closely with industry experts, students engage in hands-on projects and gain access to cutting-edge tools and technologies that provide them with practical expertise across the spectrum of interior and furniture design. This holistic approach ensures that graduates are well-prepared to make a lasting impact, with the ability to design spaces that transcend physical form and become immersive, memorable experiences.

4379.content:
### Highlights
 * The area programme consists of a well-rounded curriculum that combines both theoretical knowledge and hands-on learning, covering key areas such as spatial design, furniture design, materials and finishes, sustainability, lighting, and human-centered design.
 * Opportunities for students to work on live projects, collaborating with real clients, and creating functional and aesthetically pleasing spaces and furniture.
 * Internships, workshops, and collaborations with industry experts and renowned design studios, offering valuable insight into the latest trends and professional practices.
 * Access to advanced design software, 3D modeling tools, and fabrication workshops, enabling students to bring their concepts to life with precision.

### Area Chair Message
> Welcome to the Interior and Furniture Design program at UID, where creativity and functionality converge to transform spaces into meaningful environments.
Our programme is designed to develop professionals who excel in creating innovative spaces and crafting furniture that is not only aesthetically refined but also practical and sustainable. Through collaboration with industry experts, hands-on training with advanced tools, and immersive field trips and workshops, students gain the knowledge and skills required to excel in this dynamic field.
For those passionate about redefining spaces and designing furniture that reflects both artistry and purpose, this program provides the perfect foundation. Interior and Furniture Design is more than designing interiors or furniture - it is about shaping experiences that are thoughtful, impactful, and enduring.
##### Niraja Adloori
Associate Professor, Area Chair, Interior and Furniture Design
4381.title: About

4382.content:
#### Achievements
**Scalable Furniture:** From Concept to Creation
The Scalable Furniture project provided students with invaluable hands-on experience in full-scale furniture model-making, both in-house and within the industry. This immersive exploration focused on the mechanisms and systems used in designing multifunctional furniture for modern built environments.
Students began with concept development, delving into ideas around volume, form, function, and material. These explorations were then transformed into comprehensive design concepts, supported by detailed technical drawings that outlined materials, joinery, and assembly techniques.
The culmination of the project was the creation of a physical model, showcasing the functionality and adaptability of the furniture system. This model not only demonstrated the working mechanism but also addressed stakeholder needs and contextual requirements, offering a thoughtful and practical design solution.

The world of Fashion, Apparel and branding (Styling) has come a long way, from it being seen only as a vocational/ hobby to professional organized, popular and most importantly one of the largest employing sectors in India. Fashion Design and Styling area imbibes current industry practices into class room as live projects and case studies to learn from.
4398.title: About

4399.content:
### Highlights
 * Fashion Design and Styling has some of the most exciting practical exercises combined with research and theory.
 * Industry experts are invited to not only share their experiences but engage with students as a form of learning. During a students’ tenure multiple International and Domestic study field trips are organized such as participating at International Fashion Weeks around the globe.
 * Students get an opportunity to utilize our well-equipped labs/ studio dedicated to machinery for wood work, glass, metal, pottery, photography and leather to name a few.
4399.title: About

4400.content:
### Area Chair Message
> Our students benefit from interacting with creative industry experts whom we invite from time to time as an ongoing practice
These experts engage in workshops and help students explore many facets of Craft, apparel and design through immersive experiences. Each young creative mind is nurtured through contemporary and traditional references so they are able to problem solve and create designs worthy of balanced esthetics.
##### Ankur Gulati
Area Chair
#### Achievements
Our students are interning and securing placements with some of India’s most renowned fashion designers and sustainable product brands, collaborating with industry leaders who have showcased their work at prestigious events like Lakmé Fashion Week. With a strong track record of alumni excelling at leading brands, design studios, or establishing themselves as independent designers and entrepreneurs, we continue to foster talent that redefines creativity and innovation.
4400.title: About

4401.content:
#### Jaggery Denim Bag- Reimagining Waste
The workshop REIMAGINING WASTE successfully brought together design and animation students to explore sustainability and innovation. Participants worked with materials like Jaggery Bags, used denim, and car seat belts, transforming them into functional and creative designs that showcased the potential of upcycling and responsible material use.
Lakme Fashion Week 2024 Competition : A Group of students from Fashion Design & Styling course teamed up with a retail fashion accessory brand ‘Jaggery’ specializing in sustainable methods of reusing car seat belts and used packaging materials. Fashion students developed and produced a collection of garments that would compliment accessories by Jaggery. Shortlisted as finalists the products were showcased at Lakme
4401.title: About

4402.content:
#### The Bhuj Trip

The Craft Immersion Trip was designed to provide fashion design students with a unique opportunity to explore the rich heritage of Indian traditional crafts. The objective was to immerse them in the techniques, materials, and cultural significance of various crafts, fostering a deeper understanding of their artistry. The journey included hands-on sessions with Shyam Ji Vankar, offering insights into the intricate art of weaving, and a visit to the stunning Salt Desert (Rann of Kutch). Students attended an expert session at the iconic Parag Mahal, led by the Qasab Foundation, where they were introduced to local Banjara women and their curated works. The experience continued with a workshop at Sidr Craft, where students discovered the exquisite techniques of Bandhani dyeing, followed by a visit to local markets and a tour of the iconic Smriti Van Earthquake Museum and Miyawaki Forest
4402.title: About

4403.content:
#### The Bhuj Trip

. The trip also included an enriching visit to the workplace of Sufiyan Khatri, where students observed the meticulous processes of Ajrakh printing, and concluded with a site visit to the Khamir Craft Resource Centre. This immersive experience offered students unparalleled exposure to India’s traditional crafts, blending creativity, culture, and hands-on learning.
4403.title: About

4404.content:
#### The Bhuj Trip

> UID NCR students proudly secured the Second Prize at the Fashion Show (Open Theme) during The Damru Fest hosted by Rishihood University.This remarkable achievement highlights their creativity, innovation, and the rich learning experiences they gain through immersive journeys to craft clusters across India.
4404.title: About

### Department of Aerospace

The Aerospace Department offers B.Tech, M.Tech, and Ph.D. programmes with specialisations in Aeronautics, Astronautics, Avionics, UAVs, Defense Technologies, and Computational Fluid Dynamics. Unique pathways such as the B.Tech with Pilot Training integrate engineering with a Commercial Pilot License abroad, preparing students for careers in aviation, space exploration, and defense.
With the Aviation programs you can study and become an Aviation Professional with a CPL Pilot License in 3 years and can get your dream aviation job. With global partnerships, research-driven curricula, and hands-on training, the department positions graduates for leadership in the aerospace industry.

 * Strong industry and international linkages, including internships and opportunities to study or conduct research abroad.
 * “Pathway to Pilot” programme that integrates flight-training with the undergraduate curriculum.

 * Research labs, projects, and exposure to real-world applications from early semesters.

To train professionals who can contribute to India’s emergence as a global aerospace powerhouse — in aviation, space exploration, defense technologies, avionics, and beyond — while equipping them with the technical depth, innovation mindset, and global perspective needed to excel throughout their careers.

### Department of Energy

The Energy Department offers B.Tech, M.Tech and Ph.D. programmes with specialisations in Renewable Energy and Nuclear Energy. Students benefit from a distinctive model that combines study in India with international internships or partner-university experiences.
Emphasising sustainability and advanced energy systems, the department prepares graduates to address global energy challenges through innovation, research, and industry engagement.
#### Key Features & Advantages
 * Dual specialisation allowing students to focus on either renewable or nuclear energy depending on their interests and career goals.
 * Global exposure through study abroad programmes and international internships, enhancing practical and cross-cultural competence.
 * Strong research emphasis: energy systems, sustainability, and evolving technologies form core pillars.
4438.title: About

4439.content:
#### Mission & Vision
To foster expertise and leadership in energy engineering that balances innovation, sustainability, and societal impact. The department is dedicated to training engineers and researchers who can address the energy needs of the present and design the energy systems of the future — whether in renewables, nuclear energy, or hybrid systems.
4439.title: About

4440.content:
### Programmes Offered
 * **B.Tech in Energy Engineering:** This program is designed to create the energy professionals of the future. The students will get a comon course for the first two years and they can specialize in Renewable Energy, Nuclear Energy or in Power Systems in their last two years. In the final year they can go for a year abroad study program or go for a 6 months exhange or internship abroad.
 * **M.Tech in Renewable Energy :** The first year is based at GD Goenka; the second year includes study abroad for a year or a 6-month international/industrial internship.
 * **M.Tech in Nuclear Energy The** First year is based at GD Goenka; the second year includes study abroad for a year or a 6-month international/industrial internship.

4469.content:
### Call for Research Papers
**Paper format**
 * The paper size is A4, Margins are 4 cm (top), 2.5 cm (left and right) and 2.7 cm (bottom).
 * There are no page numbers, headers or footers on the paper.
 * Text is single spaced, not double spaced. All fonts are embedded.
 * All pages are portraits (landscape pages should be rotated).
 * The abstract text should be indented 25 mm from the left margin and there should be 10 mm space after the abstract before you begin the main text of your article, starting on the same page as the abstract.
4469.title: Conferences

4470.content:
### Call for Research Papers

**Paper content**
 * Please submit full length paper
 * The paper includes the author’s name(s), affiliation(s) and email(s). Corresponding author must be highlighted by (*).
 * All articles must contain an abstract maximum of 200 words.
 * All figures and tables should be numbered in numerical order. Please ensure that figure/table numbers are not duplicated or missed.
 * Figures are legible and placed within the text, not collected at the end of the document.
 * If section headings are numbered, ensure that they are numbered numerically, and no numbers are duplicated or missing.
 * Displayed equations should follow a naming convention in numerical order, i.e. (1), (2), (3) etc or by section, i.e. (1.1), (1.2) etc. Ensure every displayed equation has its own number and none are duplicated or missing.
 * Reference lists are checked for accuracy.
4470.title: Conferences

4471.content:
### Call for Research Papers

* Reference lists are checked for accuracy.
 * If numbering references (Harvard system) ensure that references are numbered numerically, every reference has its own number, and no numbers are duplicated or missing.
 * Ensure that all references are cited in the text and that all citations have a corresponding reference.
 * Finally, please ensure that the paper is thoroughly proofread to check the standard of English and ensure wording is clear and concise.
4471.title: Conferences

4472.content:
### Call for Research Papers

**Tracks**
 * **Track 1 –** ESG Integration in Occupational Health, Safety, Fire, and Environmental Governance.

4511.content:
### GD Goenka Sohna Marathon

Print
**GD GOENKA SOHNA MARATHON**
With agile mind and enthusiastic spirit, GD Goenka University, Gurugram organized a mega Sohna Marathon on 15 February 2020. Marking its inception this year, ‘Sohna Marathon’ is a deeply deliberated event for keeping the classic tradition of a thoughtful phrase, ‘Health is wealth’ alive and intact. The marathon aimed to aggravate the adrenaline rush, while translating a dream of healthy life into reality. The event marked the gracious presence of our eminent and esteemed dignitaries of GD Goenka University, including Mr. Rohit Gujral, Director, GD Goenka Group; Dr. Suku Bhaskaran, President; Dr. Jayasankar Variyar, Pro-Vice Chancellor; Maj. Karttikeya Sharma, Administrator and Dr. Tanuja Kaushik, Dean, Student Welfare & International Relations.
4511.title: News

4512.content:
### GD Goenka Sohna Marathon

The esteemed Guests of Honour for the Marathon were Shri. Sanjay Singh, MLA, Sohna; Ms. Pritam Rani Siwach, Former Captain, Indian Women’s Hockey Team; Ms. Sonal Dahiya, News Anchor and Producer and Dr. Hemant Singh Beniwal, Psychologist and a passionate marathon runner. With their keen and proactive spirit, they channelized more energy amidst the overwhelming euphoria of the marathon, and reiterated the importance of such an event that can constructively create iron-jawed individuals for providing a concrete base for a healthy and enlightened society.
4512.title: News

4513.content:
### GD Goenka Sohna Marathon

The theme for this year’s marathon was – RUN FOR WOMEN’S SAFETY, envisioned to respect and promote women’s empowerment, with a stressful concern for their safety. The event emphasized upon removing the barriers of unsafe environment for women, to ensure effective articulation of their potential and skills in the ever-growing contemporary scenario. The event saw a large pool of participants, nearly 1700 people, young and old, encompassing all layers of society, coming together on a common platform to stand tall in accentuating this noble and healthy cause. This event was even more special, as GD Goenka Group marks its 25 years of excellence in 2020, the silver jubilee of the Goenkan fraternity overwhelms each and every heart, while ardently striving for more milestones ahead.
4513.title: News

4514.content:
### GD Goenka Sohna Marathon

The mega marathon included four categories, the Half Marathon was of 21.1 km for the age group 18 years and above. Then, we had the Run for 10 km for age group 15 years and above. The third Run was of 5 km for the age group 10-14 years. And lastly, we had the Walkathon of 3 km for people of age 35 years and above. The route for the Sohna Marathon was an ideal picturesque view, enwrapping the Aravalli to render an awakened sense of tranquility as the feet talked with the intricacies and subtleties of the simple, yet profoundly meditative nature.
4514.title: News

4515.content:
### GD Goenka Sohna Marathon

The Sohna Marathon began with a warm welcome for our Guests of Honour, and the opening ceremony also witnessed a Zumba performance coordinated by Fitness Group of Zubair Rana, who undoubtedly accelerated the energy, beautifully pumping the blood for the run ahead. Everyone grooved and jumped on their beats, leaving the crowd roaring and rejoiced. Amidst this loud cheer, the flag was hoisted and the moment marked the beginning of the various categories of marathon for our participants.
4515.title: News

4516.content:
### GD Goenka Sohna Marathon

In the 21.1 km Run, for 18 Years & above, male category, first prize was won by Kuldeep Singh, second by Stephen Kosgei and third by Laxman Kumar Saini. In the female category, first prize was won by Rimpi Devi, second by Supriya and third by Shipra Makhija. Next, in the 10 km Run for age 15 Years & above, male category, first prize went to Avdesh Nagar, second to Meraj and third to Raju. In the female category, first position was won by Badho, second by Ekta Rawat and third by Priyanka Bhati. In the 5 Km Run for age 10 to 14 Years, male category, first prize was bagged by Lalit Kumar, second by Chintu and third by Sahil Khan. In the female category, first prize was won by Himani Raghav, second by Avni Suri and third by Ritika. All the winners got Medals and tempting cash prizes as an ode to their marvelous victory and sportsmanship.
4516.title: News

4517.content:
### GD Goenka Sohna Marathon

The event culminated itself with a Vote of Thanks by Maj. Karttikeya Sharma, Administrator, GD Goenka University; he joyously thanked all the participants and the organizers for such a remarkable event. A dance performance by GD Goenka University’s Students ended the event on an enchanting note. Everyone left with a warm smile, while ruminating about the next annual Marathon, with promising efforts and rejuvenating spirit.
4517.title: News

4581.content:
### Prof. (Dr.) Ugur Guven is an Aerospace Engineer (Ph.D.), and a Nuclear Engineer (MSc), and his area of specialization is Nuclear Rocket Propulsion and Interstellar Travel. During his 28 years of career, he has published over 25 books, over 100 journal papers, and 250+ conference papers.

Dr. Guven served as the Advisory Council Member of the UN Center for Science and Technology Education in the Asia Pacific Region from 2015 to 2022, and he actively participates in NASA focus group meetings such as LEAG. Dr. Guven is the Founder and Director of the Indo-French Academic Alliance, and he is currently in the process of forming the Indo- French Aerospace Consortium. 4618.content:
### About the Conference
TLASH 2.0 , hosted by GD Goenka University, will build on the success of TLASH 2024 to further explore the role of higher education institutions in advancing Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The conference will bring together scholars, policymakers, and industry leaders to discuss innovative strategies for integrating SDGs into education, research, and institutional policies. Through meaningful deliberations by SMEs, panel discussions, poster presentations, and research presentations, TLASH 2.0 aims to showcase best practices, strengthen global collaborations, and address emerging challenges in sustainability. With a strong focus on actionable solutions, this event will serve as a platform for meaningful dialogue and transformative initiatives in higher education.
4618.title: Conferences

4619.content:
### Objectives
 * To further the transformative potential of SDGs and the role of HEIs in achieving them.
 * To showcase successful initiatives and best practices by HEIs in integrating SDGs into their teaching, research, and community engagement activities.
 * To foster collaboration and partnerships between HEIs, governments, the private sector, and civil society organizations to accelerate progress towards the SDGs.
 * To identify challenges and opportunities in mainstreaming SDGs within higher education.
 * To develop recommendations for a comprehensive action plan for HEIs to contribute effectively to the 2030 Agenda.

### Guidelines for poster
Poster participants are expected to follow the following guidelines for poster making.
**Font size and type:**
 * Use font either Arial or Times New Roman throughout the poster and avoid fancy fonts.
 * All headings except for topic title should be 36 font size and in bold, capital letters.
 * Subheadings font size should be 30 pt., bold and in all capital letters.
 * References and Acknowledgments font size should be 20 pt.
 * Text should be 20 to 26 pt, which should be visible from 3-6 feet (1-2 meters) distance. Avoid lengthy notes.
 * The poster board should be not more than 0.95 meter (95 cm), wide by 1.2 meter and height (120 cm).

4691.content:
### Research
Anjali Vyass research involves Performance Analysis of Solar Air Heater to enhance the Heat transfer rate using Artificial Roughness. Her Research work deals with an Experimentation on solar air heater to find out enhancement in efficiency due to artificial roughness on absorber plate. Perforated baffles have been used as artificial roughness which is attached underneath the absorber plate of the duct. Thermal performance analysis of solar air heater was carried out for ranging Reynolds number 3000 , 11000 and results were validated in ANSYS Fluent module. Performance evaluation of solar air heater with provision of baffles to the air passage area was the main focus of the work.
4691.title: Dr. Anjali Vyas

4692.content:
### Research

An attempt has been made to produce thermal performance analysis to determine fluid flow and heat transfer characteristics of solar air heater. Artificial roughness is used in solar air heater absorber plate to break laminar boundary sub layer. It enhances rate of heat transfer from the absorber plate to the over flowing air stream. Heat transfer to the air flow in rectangular ducts with perforated baffles attached to one of the broad walls. The duct has width-to-height ratio of 7.77; the baffle pitch to height ratio is 29; the baffle height-to- duct height ratio is 0.495. It was proven beyond doubt that solar air heaters with the baffles can efficiently promote air turbulence, thereby increasing the heat transfer coefficient and efficiency.
4692.title: Dr. Anjali Vyas

> Integrating Indian Knowledge Systems: Bridging Heritage and Modern Education
## About the Centre of Indian Knowledge systems
Centre of Indian Knowledge systems (CIKS) at GD Goenka University is dedicated to promoting and preserving India’s rich intellectual heritage. The centre serves as a hub for interdisciplinary learning, integrating ancient wisdom with contemporary knowledge to address modern challenges. Through specialized courses, workshops, and research initiatives, the centre aims to foster intellectual inquiry, critical thinking, and a deeper appreciation of India's knowledge traditions.
## Vision
The vision of CIKS is to rejuvenate and mainstream Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) for the contemporary world in alignment with societal needs. The centre seeks to bridge the gap between traditional wisdom and modern disciplines, ensuring the relevance of IKS in today's academic and professional landscapes.
4841.title: LKS Lab

> CIKS aligns with the objectives set by the UGC-IKS Division, Ministry of Education, Government of India, emphasizing:
 * Parampara – The continuous knowledge traditions of Bharata since time immemorial.

 * Laukika Prayojana – Practical applications of IKS to solve contemporary and emerging global challenges.

Print
GD Goenka University, recognized by the UGC, and a member of prestigious institutions like the Association of Indian Universities (AIU), the Association of Commonwealth Universities (ACU) and the International Association of Universities (IAU), organized the 10th edition of its Annual Convocation on 22 November 2024.
The event was graced by esteemed dignitaries, including the Chief Guest, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Hon’ble Minister of Culture and Tourism and the Guest of Honour, General VK Singh (Retd.) The Convocation was a grand affair and saw 1491 graduands being awarded, out of which 598 were graduates, 602 postgraduates, 52 Diploma, and 35 Ph.D. degrees in various disciplines The event also had a total of 99 awardees for the prestigious Gopi Ram Goenka medals which included 53 Gold Medalists, 34 silver medalists and 12 bronze medalists. The highlight of the day was the conferment of Honoris Causa on Shri. Nakul Anand, Former Executive Director ITC Limited, who shared profound insights from his distinguished career. The Chief Guest of the event was Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Minister of Information & Broadcasting and Youth Affairs & Sports, Government of India. The event saw the presence of senior management from GD Goenka Group gracing the occasion which included Hon’ble Chancellor Ms. Renu Goenka, Hon’ble Pro-Chancellor Shri Nipun Goenka, the Executive Director GD Goenka Group, Mrs. Radhika Goenka and Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kim Menezes

## About The Conference
With an objective to raise the standards of Clinical Legal Education in India, the GD Goenka University, School of Law announces 2ndGDGU International Virtual Law and Technology Moot Court Competition, 2021 in association with Cyber Law University, on 28th& 29th August 2021. Moot Court Competitions, which is a mandatory part of the law curriculum in our law school offers a practical and application-based approach to learning law. It gives the law students, the necessary free space to interpret and analyze legal provisions in the context of a given legal regime while trying to solve a practical problem. The GDGU School of Law is dedicated to promoting this aspect of legal training for ensuring a wholesome legal education and the GD Goenka Virtual Moot Competition is an endeavor of the School of Law in this direction.
5169.title: Conferences

5170.content:
## About The Conference

2ndGDGU International Virtual Law and Technology Moot Court Competition, 2021 in association with Cyber Law University is about technology law. Technology law focuses on intellectual property rights, a complex branch of the legal system that deals with disputes over who ‘owns’ intangible ‘property’, such as creative works, patents, copyrights, and trade secrets. Technology law helps protect the creatives who come up with these ideas and also ensures rights concerning the distribution of their work.

5270.content:
# Dr. Debarka Mukhopadhyay

Dr. Debarka Mukhopadhyay is an academician with over twenty years of experience, including more than a decade in academic administration, along with extensive teaching and research expertise. He is currently serving as a Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at GD Goenka University, Gurgaon.
He holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science & Engineering from Maulana Abul Kalam Azad University of Technology, West Bengal, and an M.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering from Kalyani Government Engineering College under West Bengal University of Technology.
Dr. Mukhopadhyay has made significant contributions to research and innovation, with 11 granted Indian patents and 9 additional patents published and under examination. His scholarly output includes 33 conference publications, 21 SCI/Scopus-indexed journal articles, 12 book chapters, and one edited book.
5270.title: Dr. Debarka Mukhopadhyay

5271.content:
# Dr. Debarka Mukhopadhyay

He has successfully supervised one Ph.D. scholar, while two scholars have submitted their synopsis, and four are currently pursuing doctoral research under his guidance.
His current research interests encompass Quantum Computing, Quantum Deep Learning, and Quantum-Inspired Drug Discovery, with a focused emphasis on designing molecular prototypes for greenhouse gas absorption to address climate change challenges.
An enthusiastic and result-oriented professional, Dr. Mukhopadhyay is committed to advancing cutting-edge research and fostering academic excellence.

B.Sc. (PCM) - CSJM University, M.Sc. (Chemistry) - CSJM University, PhD (Chemistry) IIT Kanpur, CSIR-NET-JRF (Chemical Sciences), GATE (Chemistry)

### Overview of Research Group:
Our research group is focused on developing innovative materials and therapeutic strategies by leveraging the principles of molecular self-assembly and green chemistry. Our work is primarily centered on three key areas: photosensitive peptides, sustainable nanoparticle synthesis, and novel cancer therapies.
5395.title: Dr. Shradhey Gupta

5396.content:
### Photosensitive Peptides and Self-Assembly
We explore how light can be used to control the behavior of photosensitive peptides. These molecules can change their shape and properties when exposed to light, allowing us to precisely direct their self-assembly into complex nanostructures. A key focus is on using symmetrical covalent linkers to enhance the peptides' flexibility and responsiveness to external stimuli, such as light, temperature, and pH. The resulting materials have tunable properties, making them promising for applications in the bio-nano field. Additionally, we are investigating the potential of these photoactive molecules for the early detection of diseases like Alzheimer's.
5396.title: Dr. Shradhey Gupta

5397.content:
### Greener and Biogenic Synthesis of Nanoparticles
Our group is committed to developing environmentally friendly methods for creating nanoparticles. We use biogenic materials, such as leaf extracts, to act as scaffolds for nanoparticle formation. This sustainable approach avoids the harsh chemicals and energy-intensive processes of traditional synthesis. Our goal is to create a wide range of nanoparticles with diverse applications, including catalysis, drug delivery, and sensing, all while minimizing environmental impact.
5397.title: Dr. Shradhey Gupta

5398.content:
### Plinabulin Derivatives for Cancer Therapy and Detection
We are actively synthesizing photoactive derivatives of Plinabulin, a compound known for its promise in treating cancer, particularly lung cancer. By making these derivatives responsive to light, we can achieve highly targeted and precise therapeutic effects. This research aims to combine both cancer therapy and early detection into a single, light-activated molecule. Our ultimate goal is to develop a novel approach to lung cancer treatment and diagnosis that is both effective and non-invasive.
5398.title: Dr. Shradhey Gupta

Dr. Mishra holds a Master’s degree from the Indian Institute of Technology and a Bachelor's degree from Jadavpur University in India.

# Dr. Priya Goyal

Dr. Priya Goyal is a seasoned academician with over 18 years of experience in teaching and research in Computer Science and Engineering. She earned her Doctorate of Philosophy in CSE from MVN University and M. Tech (CSE), B.E(IT) from MDU Rohtak. Currently serving as Associate Professor in Department of Computer Science Engineering in G. D. Goenka University, Gurugram. Prior to this she was serving as Assistant Professor (Selection Grade-III) in the Department of CSE (AIML) at Manipal University Jaipur, she has previously held key roles including Head of Department and academic coordinator in reputed institutions.

Her teaching expertise spans core and advanced subjects such as Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data Analytics, and Software Engineering. Dr. Priya is actively involved in academic leadership through curriculum design, examination coordination, and policy formation. She also mentors undergraduate and postgraduate students, guiding projects that have been published and presented internationally
A passionate educator and innovator, she holds multiple patents in AI, ML, and security, and is a reviewer and committee member in leading international conferences. Her pedagogical methods aim not only to teach core concepts but also to inspire students to explore new ideas and techniques, aligning with the latest industry trends and technological advancements.

> Dr. Ugur Guven, Senior Professor of Aerospace Engineering, leads the department with expertise in interstellar travel and nuclear propulsion for space missions and habitats.
He serves on the Advisory Council of the UN CSSTEAP, promoting global aerospace education, and is the Honorary Executive Coordinator of the Indo-French Academic Alliance, helping form the Indo-French Aerospace Consortium. His research inspires innovation in deep space exploration, while his mentorship fosters hands-on learning and global engagement. ### HoD's Profile
> Dr. Sudipta K. Mishra is currently working as a Professor of Civil Engineering. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Iowa in the United States, focusing on modelling water and nutrient flow.
Dr. Mishra holds a Master’s degree from the Indian Institute of Technology and a Bachelor's degree from Jadavpur University in India.
Dr. Mishra’s research covers a broad range of critical areas within environmental and civil engineering and spans climate change impacts, groundwater modelling, urban sustainability, and the Water Energy Food (WEF) nexus. Dr. Mishra has over thirty publications, has worked in multiple funded projects, guided several Ph.D. scholars, reviews for reputed journals, and has been part of societies like ASCE and AGU. With extensive experience in construction, quality assurance, and quality control (QA/QC), Dr. Mishra brings a diverse skill set to academia.
